title: An Integrated Vision-and-Language Pretraining (VLP) and Visual Question Answering (VQA) model to Automate Nondestructive Evaluation Image Analysis
abstract: An AI-based approach called ChatNDE Figure to Caption is introduced, which aims to automate the interpretation of NDE images using deep learning and natural language processing (NLP). A Vision-and-Language Pretraining (VLP) strategy is developed to help the model learn how to connect visual features with meaningful language. Basically, we built a large NDE image dataset, trained the model using annotated examples, and then evaluated how well it performed using BLEU scores to compare its output to expert written descriptions. So, the system combines a ResNet50 model to extract important features from the images and a GPT2 language model to turn those features into natural sounding text. Even though the accuracy of the model has been low the generated caption results have been solid so far, the captions were shorter but mentioned some important features of images what human experts would say, which shows the model is learning to pick up on key details. Also, a Visual Question Answering (VQA) model is used as part of the system. VQA models are designed to take an image and a question about that image (like Is there a crack? or Where is the defect located?) and generate a useful answer. By adding this layer, the platform will not just describe what it sees, it can also respond to specific questions, making it even more interactive and helpful for inspectors in the field. This whole approach is a big step toward speeding up NDE workflows, reducing human error, and making the technology more accessible.

title: Quantum Natural Gradient on Quotient Spaces
abstract: A parametrized quantum circuit reports its state geometry through a quantum Fisher information matrix (QFIM), often singular. A small Fisher value can reflect exact state-preserving redundancy, compression by the circuit chart, or weak intrinsic distinguishability, and these mechanisms call for different numerical treatments. We show that the circuit metric factors as $F=B^{*}MB$, where $B$ is the state-level circuit-to-orbit differential and $M$ is the intrinsic Fisher operator on the reachable orbit. The factorization identifies the exact kernel as $\ker B$, separates coordinate transfer from intrinsic geometry, and yields the condition for a circuit to realize an orbit-level quantum natural-gradient (QNG) direction. When the prescribed redundancy exhausts the Fisher kernel, the Moore--Penrose update is the minimum-norm horizontal lift of the quotient Riemannian gradient. At critical points with a locally diffeomorphic quotient-to-orbit map, chart singular values cancel from the linearized QNG operator while intrinsic anisotropy remains; in the trace-orthonormal full-control generator frame, excitation-gap anisotropy gives $κ_{\mathrm{QNG}}=κ_{\mathrm{Eucl}}$. Representation theory makes $M$ explicit on highest-weight, Slater, and fermionic-Gaussian orbits, and cominuscule fidelity flow becomes integrable, with conserved principal-defect ratios, cubic Lie-retracted convergence at $η=2$, and stability boundary $η=4$. Finite data impose a second boundary: an estimated QFIM and its confidence radius alone cannot distinguish an exact zero from a small physical mode, so the estimated spectrum alone cannot license hard projection. Under depolarization, inverse-Fisher scaling amplifies mean updates and fluctuations together and cannot restore update signal-to-noise. A redundant Slater/Givens circuit confirms exact transfer identities and illustrates finite-shot tradeoffs.

title: How Identity and Opinion Shape Political Sycophancy in LLMs
abstract: As Large Language Models (LLMs) increasingly encourage users to disclose personal profiles for tailored assistance, measuring their political alignment becomes increasingly important. However, many existing benchmarks for assessing political behavior rely on closed-ended questions and do not fully capture how a model's stance may adapt to user-provided context during interaction. We introduce a framework that disentangles two distinct triggers of political sycophancy: opinion (aligning with explicit narratives) and identity (stereotyping based on demographic labels). Using 450 manually-checked political dilemmas as controlled probes, we evaluate 13 instruction-tuned LLMs. We uncover a dissociation: a model's susceptibility to explicit opinions does not necessarily predict its susceptibility to identity cues, and vice versa. When both signals are present, their effects are generally sub-additive rather than simply additive. Additionally, system-level personas primarily shift a model's baseline stance while having limited effect on the stance shift caused by user opinion or identity. Ultimately, our results suggest that LLM political stance is interactively and steerably vulnerable rather than being a fixed trait, highlighting how personalization may amplify identity- or opinion-conditioned shifts in the model's behaviors.

title: Local Patterns and the Cost of Costas Array Search
abstract: We restrict Costas-array search at a new order using seven-dotdifference signatures observed at smaller orders. At order 28, avocabulary built only from the 204 arrays of order 27 recovers 67 ofthe 89 known classes, up to rotations and reflections.Ten controls containing the same number of signatures generatedfrom valid random prefixes recover none. In experiments at orderswith complete catalogs, 592 of 633 recovered classes ($93.5\%$) aresporadic under our conservative classification. Because $97.8\%$ ofthe known classes at orders 9--23, which contribute all but three ofthe recovered classes, are sporadic, this describes theoutput composition, not a preference of the filter. Completed sweepswithin explicitly restricted search spaces at orders 30 and 31 returnexactly the predicted known arrays and no others. At order 32, thecorresponding restricted search space is empty; the full order remainsopen. Released implementations support a sampled estimate of 43.7 CPUyears for unrestricted search at order 28 and a GPU projection of 7.97GPU years at order 30.

title: Scaling Intermediate-Task Data Size for Zero-Shot Cross-Lingual Transfer in mT5 Models
abstract: Intermediate-task training---fine-tuning a pretrained model on an intermediate task before fine-tuning again on the target task---often improves model performance substantially on language understanding tasks in monolingual English settings. We investigate whether English intermediate-task training is still helpful on non-English target tasks. Using nine intermediate language-understanding tasks, we evaluate intermediate-task transfer in a zero-shot cross-lingual setting on the XTREME benchmark. We see large improvements from intermediate training on the BUCC and Tatoeba sentence retrieval tas Research goal: Does scaling the intermediate-task training data size affect the zero-shot cross-lingual transfer accuracy of mT5 models on XTREME-R tasks, and what is the optimal dataset size for maximal performance? Autonomous synthesis report generated by Assignee Research. Tribunal consensus score: 9.2/10.

title: The Descent of Learning: A Narrative Review of Stochastic Optimization, from Robbins and Monro to AdamW
abstract: The optimizer is the engine of learning: the algorithm that turns gradients into parameter updates, and whose history is the machine learning's longest engineering argument about how fast to trust a noisy direction. This article presents a narrative review of the primary literature of that argument, from Robbins and Monro's stochastic approximation---the 1951 theorem that a noisy gradient followed at a shrinking step converges to the root---through Polyak's momentum, which accelerated descent by averaging recent gradients, Nesterov's accelerated gradient, which certified the convergence rate O(1/k$^2$), Rumelhart, Hinton, and Williams's back-propagation, which put stochastic gradient descent at the heart of neural learning, and Bottou's large-scale SGD, which made the noise a resource, to the adaptive methods of the 2010s---Duchi, Hazan, and Singer's AdaGrad, Zeiler's ADADELTA, Tieleman and Hinton's RMSprop, Kingma and Ba's Adam---and the corrections that disciplined them: Sutskever, Martens, Dahl, and Hinton on initialization and momentum, Reddi, Kale, and Kumar on Adam's convergence, and Loshchilov and Hutter's AdamW, which decoupled weight decay. The synthesis is organized around three themes: the noise contract, in which the stochastic step was proven to converge and then reinterpreted as an asset of large-scale learning; the adaptivity program, in which per-parameter learning rates were derived from gradient histories; and the correction cycle, in which momentum was reanalyzed and Adam's counterexamples repaired. It is concluded that the optimizer's literature is machine learning's most cumulative lineage---each method a revision of the previous contract---and that the descent of learning, from Robbins and Monro's shrinking steps to AdamW's decoupled decay, remains the field's load-bearing mathematics.

title: Uni-mHC: Unistochastic Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections with Quantum-Interference Disentanglement
abstract: Manifold-constrained hyper-connections (mHC) stabilize deep multi-stream residual training by projecting the inter-stream mixing matrix onto the Birkhoff polytope of doubly stochastic matrices via Sinkhorn–Knopp iterations. Entrywise non-negativity, however, restricts mixing to additive convex combinations: features can never be subtracted, a limitation recently criticized in the signed-hyper-connections (sHC) line of work. We propose Uni-mHC, which lifts the constraint manifold from the Birkhoff polytope to the unistochastic set: a complex Cayley transform of a skew-Hermitian parameter matrix yields a unitary U whose modulus square S = |U|⊙|U| is doubly stochastic by construction—no projection, no iteration. Macroscopically S preserves exact energy conservation; microscopically a heterodyne readout W = Re(U eiφ) admits negative effective weights through destructive (phase-π) interference while remaining row-wise non-expansive. On a controlled subtractive task (Y = X₀−X₁), non-negative baselines plateau at the theoretical floor ½Var(Y)≈0.99 whereas Uni-mHC converges to 1.1×10−11; the operator is also the fastest and constraint-exact of all compared parameterizations, and the identity-initialized four-stream topology—instantiated here with Uni-mHC—reaches 2.3× lower validation loss than an identically trained vanilla GPT. Code (MIT) and full training logs are in the supplementary ZIP. Chinese pen name: 暮迟 (DDDMUC), Independent Researcher.

title: Christoffel-Symbol-Encoded Geodesics on Quantum Hardware: Toward an Experimental Platform for Curvature-Quantum Interplay
abstract: Overview This Zenodo repository contains the research artifacts associated with the manuscript: “Christoffel-Symbol-Encoded Geodesics on Quantum Hardware: Toward an Experimental Platform for Curvature-Quantum Interplay” The repository accompanies the APS journal submission and contains the submission manuscript, computational notebook, experimental run notes, quantum circuit files, an interactive HTML module, and handwritten theoretical and conceptual notes developed during the research. These materials are provided to support transparency, reproducibility, verification, and further exploration of the proposed framework for encoding Christoffel-symbol information into quantum circuits and studying geodesic dynamics on quantum hardware. Note: This archive contains the APS submission draft and research-development artifacts. Some files are working notes, intermediate materials, or experimental documentation and should not be interpreted as part of the final published version of the manuscript. Repository Contents 1. APS Submission Draft The Submission Draft_Final folder contains the manuscript and supporting notes associated with the APS journal submission. The primary manuscript is: ChristoffelSymbolEncoding_Final_submission_draft.pdf This PDF contains the manuscript prepared for submission to the APS journal. The folder also contains supporting documentation associated with the reported experimental results. 2. Computational Notebook The repository contains: Geodesic.ipynb This Jupyter Notebook contains computational material associated with the proposed framework and the analysis of the experimental results. The notebook includes calculations and analysis used during the development and evaluation of the Christoffel-symbol-encoded geodesic circuits. The notebook represents a research and submission working artifact and is included to document the computational workflow and analysis. The notebook can be opened using: Jupyter Notebook JupyterLab Google Colab Other compatible Jupyter environments 3. Interactive HTML Module The HTML_file folder contains an interactive HTML implementation of the setup described in the manuscript. The HTML module is designed so that users can download it and interact with or modify the setup locally without requiring an account or login. Using the HTML module Download the HTML_file folder from this repository. Open the included index.html file in a modern web browser. Explore the interactive setup. Modify the available parameters/settings directly in the interactive module. Use the modified configuration to explore how changes affect the corresponding setup. No login or external account is required to use or modify the locally downloaded HTML module. The HTML artifact is provided as an accessible, interactive research tool intended to make the experimental setup easier to inspect and explore. Note: The HTML module is a local interactive artifact. Its behavior may depend on the browser and the capabilities implemented in the provided HTML/JavaScript files. 4. QASM Quantum Circuits The repository contains the following OpenQASM circuit files: geodesic_.qasm geodesic_schwarzschild.qasm geodesic-flat.qasm These files contain the quantum circuits used to implement and investigate the proposed geodesic encoding. The QASM files can be imported into compatible IBM Quantum/Qiskit environments, including the IBM Quantum Composer where supported, for inspection and execution. Researchers can use these files to: Inspect the circuit construction. Examine the gate-level implementation. Reproduce the circuit setup. Modify the circuits for additional experiments. Execute the circuits on compatible quantum simulators. Execute the circuits on available IBM quantum hardware. Hardware execution considerations The circuits were designed for execution on real quantum hardware. Results from subsequent executions may not be numerically identical to the results reported in the manuscript. This is expected for experiments performed on noisy quantum hardware because measured results can depend on: Hardware calibration Qubit coherence and connectivity Gate and readout errors Device noise Compilation/transpilation Backend configuration Execution date and time Number of measurement shots Therefore, the QASM files are intended to provide the reproducible circuit and experimental procedure, while acknowledging the time-dependent nature of physical quantum hardware. 5. Handwritten Theoretical and Conceptual Notes The Handwritten Theory Notes folder contains handwritten material documenting the conceptual and theoretical development of the research. The materials include: Initial theoretical ideas Derivations and calculations Circuit-design sketches Christoffel-symbol encoding concepts Spacetime and geodesic illustrations Experimental setup notes Run-specific observations Additional conceptual development related to the curvature–quantum interplay They are included to document the development of the underlying research idea and provide additional context for the methodology presented in the manuscript. These materials should be considered research-development notes rather than polished manuscript material. Experimental Run Documentation The repository includes documentation of the experimental runs used in developing and evaluating the proposed framework. The experimental artifacts include: Quantum circuit files in QASM format Computational analysis in the Jupyter notebook Run-specific written observations Handwritten experimental notes Interactive visualization and exploration of the proposed setup The run notes are included to provide additional context concerning the observed behavior of the circuits on quantum hardware. Because the experiments involve real quantum hardware, variations between executions are expected. The purpose of providing the circuit files and associated documentation is therefore to enable researchers to reproduce the experimental setup, circuit construction, and methodology, rather than to imply that every hardware execution will produce exactly identical measurement statistics. Reproducibility The artifacts in this repository are intended to facilitate independent examination and reproduction of the work. The principal reproducibility components are: Artifact Purpose Geodesic.ipynb Computational calculations and analysis .qasm files Gate-level quantum circuit implementations index.html Interactive and locally modifiable representation of the setup Submission PDF Scientific description of the proposed methodology and experiments Results notes Documentation of experimental observations Handwritten notes Conceptual and theoretical development of the approach For quantum-hardware experiments, reproducibility should be understood in the context of noisy and time-varying physical hardware. Re-execution of the same circuit can result in different measurement statistics even when the circuit parameters and experimental protocol are unchanged. Accordingly, the repository provides the information necessary to reproduce the circuit construction and experimental methodology, while hardware-dependent numerical variations should be expected. File Organization Christoffel_Symbol_Encoding_Submission/ │ ├── Geodesic.ipynb │ ├── geodesic_.qasm ├── geodesic_schwarzschild.qasm ├── geodesic-flat.qasm │ ├── HTML_file/ │ └── index.html │ ├── Handwritten Theory Notes/ │ ├── Run1.HEIC │ ├── Run2.HEIC │ ├── Page1.HEIC │ ├── Page2.HEIC │ ├── Page3.HEIC │ ├── Fig1a) Chris_Symbol_encoding.drawio.png │ └── fig2_spacetime_geodesic.png │ └── Submission Draft_Final/ ├── ChristoffelSymbolEncoding_Final_submission_draft.pdf └── Copy of Notes-on-results.docx Authors Dr. Hemanth Gudaparthi, Dr. Yacine Merdjemak The handwritten theoretical notes, conceptual sketches, and research-development materials included in this archive were prepared by Dr. Hemanth Gudaparthi during the development of the work. He also implemented the quantum circuit, applied the error-mitigation protocol, analyzed the measurement results, and wrote the manuscript Dr. Yacine Merdjemak has provided input on the reasoning, the approach, and the quantum circuit implementation, reviewed the manuscript, and commented on the theoretical framework and result interpretation. Associated Manuscript Christoffel-Symbol-Encoded Geodesics on Quantum Hardware: Toward an Experimental Platform for Curvature-Quantum Interplay The manuscript included in this repository represents the APS journal submission draft associated with these research artifacts. Please refer to the final published version of the manuscript for the authoritative bibliographic record once publication is complete. Citation If you use the computational notebooks, QASM circuits, interactive HTML module, experimental notes, handwritten notes, or other materials from this repository, please cite the associated manuscript: Hemanth Gudaparthi, Yacine Merdjemak, Christoffel-Symbol-Encoded Geodesics on Quantum Hardware: Toward an Experimental Platform for Curvature-Quantum Interplay, 2026, https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22162434 The citation should be updated to the final journal bibliographic information when the manuscript is published. Use of the Materials These materials are provided for research, educational, verification, and scholarly exploration. Users are encouraged to: Examine and modify the locally available HTML module. Inspect and modify the QASM circuits. Re-run the computational notebook. Reproduce the experimental circuit construction. Extend the framework to additional parameters, circuit depths, geometries, or quantum hardware platforms. Please cite the associated manuscript

title: Decentralized Federated Learning with Differential Privacy via Homomorphic Encryption
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to decentralized federated learning that leverages the strengths of differential privacy and homomorphic encryption to achieve robust privacy guarantees. The core idea is to encrypt each participant's local data using homomorphic encryption, allowing a central server to perform computations directly on the encrypted data without ever needing to access the plaintext. Subsequently, the encrypted results are sent back to the participants. This architecture effectively mitigates privacy risks associated with traditional federated learning methods. The combination of these three technologies – federated learning, differential privacy, and homomorphic encryption – provides a powerful framework for secure and decentralized machine learning. We demonstrate the potential for achieving strong privacy guarantees while maintaining the benefits of distributed learning.

title: Distributed Consensus with Byzantine Fault Tolerance via Quantum Key Distribution
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to distributed consensus that leverages quantum key distribution (QKD) for Byzantine fault tolerance. Traditional consensus algorithms struggle to guarantee agreement in the face of malicious actors introducing Byzantine faults. This work introduces a framework where a shared secret, established via QKD, serves as the foundation for a consensus protocol. The inherent cryptographic properties of QKD – specifically its ability to detect eavesdropping – are exploited to identify and neutralize malicious nodes attempting to disrupt the consensus process. We demonstrate that this combination offers a fundamentally more secure and efficient solution compared to classical approaches. The core of our system relies on the creation of a quantum-secured shared key, denoted as *K*, and the subsequent implementation of a consensus protocol designed to operate on this key. This protocol incorporates mechanisms for key verification and anomaly detection, providing robust resilience against Byzantine faults. The theoretical analysis presented highlights the advantages of this approach in terms of security and efficiency. We define the following key variables: *n* - number of nodes in the network; *f* - maximum number of faulty nodes; *m* - number of correct nodes; *si* - the state of node *i* (1 if active, 0 if faulty); *K* - the quantum key shared among the nodes; *ri,j* - the raw key shared between nodes *i* and *j*; *Ei,j* - the error rate observed between nodes *i* and *j* during QKD; *σi,j* - the quantum state used for key exchange between nodes *i* and *j*; *Ci,j* - the ciphertext generated during the QKD process; *Di,j* - the decrypted ciphertext between nodes *i* and *j*; *Hi,j* - the hash value calculated based on the decrypted ciphertext. The system's robustness is directly proportional to the level of security provided by QKD and the effectiveness of the consensus protocol in detecting and isolating faulty nodes.

title: Quantum Key Distribution Based on Quantum Decoherence
abstract: This paper investigates a novel approach to quantum key distribution (QKD) leveraging the phenomenon of quantum decoherence. Traditional QKD protocols, while theoretically secure, are susceptible to various attacks, often relying on the assumption of perfect quantum state preservation. This research proposes a framework for distributed key generation utilizing the inherent limitations imposed by quantum decoherence. The core concept involves encoding key information within quantum states that are deliberately designed to be vulnerable to decoherence. This vulnerability, rather than being a weakness, is exploited to introduce a level of inherent security, effectively masking the key's true value from an eavesdropper attempting to intercept and measure the quantum states. We explore the mathematical formalization of this process, detailing the generation of entangled states, the measurement protocols, and the key distillation process, all incorporating the effects of decoherence. The proposed system offers a potentially more robust defense against sophisticated attacks by introducing a naturally occurring element of uncertainty. This work provides a foundational understanding of utilizing decoherence as a key component within a QKD architecture. ---

title: Core Claim: Design a self-adaptive matrix learning algorithm that automatically adjusts matrix parameters based on data distribution, enabling more effective machine learning models and facilitating transfer to different tasks.
abstract: The field of machine learning relies heavily on the optimization of complex models, often requiring extensive tuning and adaptation to different datasets. Traditional approaches frequently suffer from suboptimal performance due to the inability to effectively incorporate data distribution shifts. This research introduces a novel self-adaptive matrix learning algorithm designed to overcome these limitations. The algorithm dynamically adjusts the matrix parameters during the training process, enabling the model to adapt to varying data distributions and facilitate efficient transfer to new tasks. We propose a method based on iterative optimization, which systematically refines the matrix parameters to minimize prediction error and maximize model generalization. The core mechanism of this algorithm involves a robust optimization framework that ensures the matrix parameters are optimized in a manner that minimizes the error across the entire training dataset. This approach contrasts with static parameter adjustment methods, which often lead to suboptimal performance in dynamic environments. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this algorithm through extensive experimentation on several benchmark datasets, showcasing improved accuracy, faster convergence, and enhanced transferability compared to existing state-of-the-art techniques. The results indicate that this self-adaptive matrix learning algorithm offers a significant advancement in machine learning model optimization, particularly when dealing with data distributions that change over time. The algorithm's adaptability and potential for transfer learning contribute to its value in various applications requiring robust and versatile machine learning solutions.

title: Quantum Computation Based on Measurement Theory
abstract: This paper proposes a novel computational model based on quantum measurement theory. The core idea is to treat computation as a series of quantum measurements, offering a potentially transformative paradigm for computing. We decompose computational tasks into sequences of measurements, leveraging mathematical tools from quantum measurement theory to perform calculations. The model explores the impact of the measurement process on computational efficiency. Unlike existing models rooted in classical physics, this approach directly addresses the fundamental role of measurement in information processing, potentially unlocking new computational possibilities. The model is presented with detailed mathematical formulations, focusing on measurement operators, state vectors, and the dynamics of measurement processes. The analysis aims to provide a theoretical framework for understanding and developing quantum computation based on the principles of measurement. ---

title: Quantum Error Correction Codes: Probabilistic Error Correction and Reconstruction
abstract: This paper investigates the application of probabilistic error correction techniques within quantum error correction codes, coupled with machine learning algorithms, to enhance the effectiveness of quantum information processing in noisy environments. Traditional quantum error correction methods primarily rely on deterministic correction mechanisms, often failing to adequately account for the probabilistic nature of noise. This work proposes a novel framework that leverages the probabilistic characteristics of quantum error correction codes, combined with machine learning, to dynamically predict noise distributions and adapt the error correction strategy. The core mechanism involves designing a probabilistic error correction policy based on the chosen quantum error correction code and employing machine learning to predict the noise distribution. This predictive capability allows for dynamic adjustment of the error correction scheme, ultimately leading to improved quantum information reconstruction. The theoretical underpinnings and algorithmic design are presented, outlining a path toward more robust quantum communication and computation. This approach offers a significant departure from conventional methods and promises to unlock greater resilience in quantum systems facing environmental noise. ---

title: Quantum Neural Networks with Non-Markovian Dynamics
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of quantum neural networks (QNNs) enhanced by non-Markovian dynamics. Traditional Markovian QNNs suffer from limitations in capturing long-range dependencies, a crucial aspect in complex data processing. We propose a novel QNN architecture that incorporates quantum memory and entanglement to facilitate non-Markovian information processing. This approach allows the network to retain and utilize the entire past history of the input, fundamentally altering the dynamics of information flow. Through theoretical analysis and mathematical formulations, we demonstrate how this architecture can significantly improve the network's ability to learn and represent complex patterns, particularly those exhibiting long-range correlations. Specifically, we introduce a modified update rule leveraging the concept of quantum memory and entanglement, expressed as: $ \Delta w_{ij} = \alpha \cdot E[\rho(t)|x_1, x_2, ..., x_K] \cdot \langle \psi_i | \rho(t) | \psi_j \rangle - (1 - \alpha) \cdot w_{ij}$ Where: * $ \Delta w_{ij}$ is the change in the synaptic weight between neurons *i* and *j*. * $\alpha$ is the learning rate. * $E[\rho(t)|x_1, x_2, ..., x_K]$ represents the expected state of the quantum memory at time *t*, given the entire input sequence $x_1, x_2, ..., x_K$. * $\rho(t)$ is the density matrix representing the quantum state at time *t*. * $\langle \psi_i | \rho(t) | \psi_j \rangle$ is the inner product between the quantum states $\psi_i$ and $\psi_j$ within the density matrix $\rho(t)$. * $w_{ij}$ is the current synaptic weight between neurons *i* and *j*. The core of our innovation lies in the utilization of quantum memory, modeled as a quantum state $\rho(t)$, which retains information about the entire past sequence. The entanglement between neurons further enables correlated updates, bypassing the limitations of Markovian models that only consider immediate dependencies. We explore the impact of varying the strength of entanglement and the capacity of the quantum memory on the network's performance using mathematical models. The results suggest a significant improvement in accuracy and convergence speed compared to standard Markovian QNNs when dealing with datasets exhibiting long-range dependencies. Further investigation into the scalability and practical implementation of this architecture is warranted.

title: How Close to the Frontier? Measuring the Fidelity of Deployable Open-weights LLMs to a Frontier Reference for Clinical Phenotype Extraction
abstract: Frontier large language models read clinical narratives at near expert level, but hospitals often cannot deploy them: privacy regulation, data-residency rules, and on-premises requirements forbid sending patient text to a cloud service.The deployable alternative is a small open-weights model run locally.We ask a scoped fidelity question: how closely do such models reproduce a frontier reference for clinical phenotype extraction (cohort identification from records, not bedside diagnosis)?On a 500-case subset of PMC-Patients and six guideline-defined cardiometabolic conditions, we place seven self-hostable open-weights models between a keyword floor and a frontier ceiling, the consensus of two frontier models.The strongest reach macro-F1 of about 0.95 against the ceiling; under a realistic deployment prompt, a 14B model matches a 70B (no significant difference), and a three-small-model ensemble significantly outscores the standalone 70B, at far lower hardware cost.Once self-hosted, a case carries no per-call cost, so deployment becomes a hardware decision.We release the benchmark, reference, and code.

title: Scaling Intermediate-Task Data Size for Zero-Shot Cross-Lingual Transfer on XTREME-R
abstract: Intermediate-task training---fine-tuning a pretrained model on an intermediate task before fine-tuning again on the target task---often improves model performance substantially on language understanding tasks in monolingual English settings. We investigate whether English intermediate-task training is still helpful on non-English target tasks. Using nine intermediate language-understanding tasks, we evaluate intermediate-task transfer in a zero-shot cross-lingual setting on the XTREME benchmark. We see large improvements from intermediate training on the BUCC and Tatoeba sentence retrieval tas Research goal: How does the scaling of intermediate-task training data size affect the zero-shot cross-lingual transfer performance on XTREME-R, measured by accuracy on adversarial examples compared to baseline multilingual pretraining? title: High-Order Quantum State Space Learning with Adaptive Topology
abstract: Quantum state space learning is a critical challenge in the development of quantum algorithms and systems. Traditional methods often lack the integration of topological information, hindering efficiency gains. This paper introduces a novel high-order quantum state space learning algorithm, integrating quantum topology information to optimize quantum system parameters and topological structure. The core mechanism leverages a tailored learning process guided by topological constraints, leading to improved performance and enhanced quantum computational capabilities. We present a comprehensive framework for dynamically adjusting the optimization process based on topological properties, resulting in a significant advancement in the efficiency of quantum state space exploration.

abstract: Quantum entanglement, a cornerstone of quantum mechanics, offers a potentially revolutionary approach to secure information transmission and processing. title: Title: Quantum-Enhanced Diffusion Process (QEP)
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of quantum-enhanced diffusion processes to revolutionize generative modeling. Traditional diffusion models, while effective, suffer from computationally intensive training times and limitations in generating diverse and accurate outputs. We propose a novel approach leveraging quantum annealing and Grover's algorithm to dramatically accelerate the diffusion process, thereby improving both speed and accuracy. This research explores the theoretical foundations of QEP, outlines the implementation details, and presents preliminary results demonstrating significant performance improvements compared to conventional diffusion methods. The core mechanism centers around quantum acceleration of the forward and reverse diffusion steps, offering a pathway to overcome limitations in traditional algorithms. The investigation touches on the implications of this technology for various generative modeling applications, including image generation and data synthesis.

abstract: This paper proposes a novel quantum neuro-morphic computing architecture designed to enhance computational efficiency and parallelism. The core concept involves integrating quantum logic gates with neural networks to create a hybrid system capable of leveraging the strengths of both paradigms. We explore the potential of this architecture to achieve significant improvements in computational performance, particularly for complex problems that benefit from parallel processing and quantum phenomena. The architecture is predicated on a fundamentally new approach to computation, moving beyond traditional von Neumann architectures and exploring the synergistic relationship between quantum and neuromorphic computing. title: Title: Quantum Entanglement-Based Topological Information Encoding
abstract: Quantum entanglement is a fundamental phenomenon in quantum mechanics with the potential for revolutionary applications in secure communication and data compression. This paper explores the design of a novel quantum entanglement encoding scheme leveraging the unique properties of entangled states. We propose a method that utilizes the inherent topological structure of quantum states to encode information, enabling robust data security and efficient compression. Furthermore, we investigate the use of topological structures to facilitate the reversible encoding and decoding process, offering a promising path toward enhanced information security. The core claim of this research is that this proposed approach offers significant advantages in terms of security and compression compared to existing methods.

title: Self-Organizing Fractal Networks for High-Dimensional Data Exploration
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to high-dimensional data exploration utilizing self-organizing fractal networks. Traditional methods often struggle with the curse of dimensionality, leading to sparsity and difficulty in identifying meaningful patterns. Fractal networks, leveraging their inherent self-similarity, offer a potential solution by creating hierarchical representations that can capture complex relationships within high-dimensional spaces. This work proposes a dynamic algorithm that constructs and refines a fractal network based on the statistical properties of the input data. The algorithm iteratively adjusts the network's topology, prioritizing connections that reflect the underlying data distribution. The core of this approach is the self-organization process, allowing the network to adapt and evolve, ultimately producing a representation that effectively captures the essential features of the data. We demonstrate the efficacy of this method through theoretical analysis and outline its potential applications in various fields. The proposed framework provides a robust and adaptive method for uncovering hidden structures in high-dimensional datasets.

title: Physics of Adaptive Modeling of Entropy Effects
abstract: This research explores the application of adaptive neural networks to simulate and predict physical systems, with a particular focus on the influence of entropy effects. The core claim is that utilizing adaptive modeling offers a more precise approach than traditional static models, especially within complex systems. We investigate a novel methodology for learning and applying these effects, aiming to capture the dynamic nature of entropy changes. The study employs a self-organizing neural network to dynamically adjust the model parameters based on observed data, demonstrating improved simulation accuracy and predictive capabilities across a range of physical scenarios. The research will analyze the impact of entropy on various physical phenomena, including fluid dynamics and thermal conductivity, highlighting the potential of this adaptive approach to enhance our understanding of complex systems.

title: Based on Quantum Entanglement, Machine Learning Knowledge Transfer
abstract: This paper introduces a novel machine learning approach for knowledge transfer, leveraging the unique properties of quantum entanglement. We propose a framework centered on exploiting entangled states to facilitate the transfer of information between domains, aiming to significantly enhance the efficiency of knowledge migration. The core mechanism utilizes quantum entanglement to establish correlations between data points, enabling the transfer of knowledge without relying on classical data pathways. This approach offers a potential paradigm shift in machine learning, particularly in scenarios demanding high-fidelity and efficient knowledge transfer across disparate domains. The paper details the theoretical framework, proposed algorithms, and preliminary experimental validation demonstrating the efficacy of this quantum entanglement-based knowledge transfer method.

title: Adaptive Probability Models: A Novel Approach to Enhanced Predictive Performance
abstract: This paper introduces an Adaptive Probability Model (APM) designed to address the limitations of traditional probability models by dynamically adjusting model parameters and structure based on the inherent information contained within the data itself. The core innovation lies in an "adaptability learning" mechanism, which automatically adjusts model parameters to better fit the data through the analysis of its "entropy" and "structure." This approach significantly improves model accuracy and generalization capabilities, particularly in scenarios involving complex and non-stationary data. The benefits of this model include improved predictive fidelity, reduced overfitting, and enhanced robustness to data variations. We present a framework demonstrating the effectiveness of this approach through a series of simulations and experiments, showcasing its superior performance compared to existing methods.

title: Design of a Compiler Optimizer Based on Simulated Annealing
abstract: This paper presents the design and implementation of a compiler optimizer utilizing the Simulated Annealing (SA) algorithm. The core aim is to enhance compiler efficiency and code performance by intelligently optimizing the instruction selection and code generation processes. The compiler optimization problem is formulated as a simulated annealing problem, enabling the SA algorithm to explore the solution space and identify optimal instruction selection and code generation schemes. The effectiveness of this approach is demonstrated through the theoretical framework and presented design. This work contributes to the growing field of applying metaheuristic optimization techniques to compiler design, offering a novel approach to achieving superior code quality and compilation speed.

title: Sentiment analysis of public opinion toward government regulations concerning the implementation of tabungan perumahan rakyat (Tapera) using the convolutional neural network (CNN) model on social media X
abstract: Sentiment analysis is one of the applications of Natural Language Processing (NLP) for identifying public opinion on social media. Although previous studies on Tapera sentiment analysis have applied conventional machine learning and transformer-based approaches, limited attention has been given to integrating automatic lexicon-based sentiment labeling with semantic word representation and deep learning classification within a unified framework. This study proposes an approach that integrates the Indonesian Sentiment Lexicon (InSet), Word2Vec, and Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) to classify public sentiment toward the Tabungan Perumahan Rakyat (Tapera) policy on social media X. A total of 1,291 tweets were processed through the preprocessing stage and automatically labeled using InSet. Word2Vec was employed to construct semantic word representations that were used as the initial weights of the CNN embedding layer. The proposed model was evaluated using four hold-out data split scenarios and compared with BiLSTM and Random Forest. The experimental results showed that the 80:20 configuration achieved the best performance with an accuracy of 74.52%, outperforming BiLSTM (71.43%) and Random Forest (69.88%). The novelty of this study lies in integrating automatic sentiment labeling using the Indonesian Sentiment Lexicon (InSet), semantic representation through Word2Vec, and CNN-based classification within a unified framework, together with an empirical evaluation of different train-test split ratios for Tapera policy sentiment analysis. These findings demonstrate that the proposed approach provides competitive sentiment classification performance while reducing dependence on manual sentiment annotation.

title: Refined Graph-Guided Fusion Network for Explainable Multimodal Lung Cancer Classification Using CT Imaging and Semantic Features
abstract: Classifying benign and malignant lung nodules from computed tomography (CT) images remains difficult because lung nodules can be hard to classify, and unimodal models cannot capture complementary diagnostic information. Despite the success of deep learning, existing methods rely only on image information and miss semantic information that can be obtained from an expert radiologist’s knowledge. Hence, the authors propose a new multimodal lung nodule classification model in this study, named the Graph-Guided Fusion Network (R-GGFN), that combines three-dimensional (3D) CT image features and structured radiologist annotations. The proposed architecture consists of three models. A 3D ResNet-18 network for image feature extraction, an MLP network for encoding semantic information, and a Graph Attention Network (GAT) for capturing inter-nodule relationships and fusing multimodal information with the graph. We add a tabular skip connection to preserve discriminative semantic features and use focal loss to address imbalance during training. To prevent data leakage, we partitioned the publicly available LIDC-IDRI dataset at the patient level. Experimental results on a held-out patient-level test set, accessed only once after model selection was finalized, show that the proposed R-GGFN achieves an accuracy of 85.21%, an AUROC of 0.9147, a PR-AUC of 0.9213, and an F1-score of 0.8609. Among all unimodal and multimodal baselines internally evaluated, R-GGFN achieved the best value on every reported metric, including accuracy, AUROC, PR-AUC, F1-score, Precision, sensitivity, and specificity. Furthermore, the proposed approach enhances model transparency by combining explainable AI techniques (e.g., 3D Grad-CAM, SHAP, and graph visualization) to explain the model at the image, feature, and graph levels. The results show that the graph-guided multimodal fusion method can fully leverage complementary image and semantic information, improving diagnostic accuracy and interpretability. The framework proposed here is a good and understandable computer-aided diagnosis decision-support system for lung cancer and a step towards future external dataset validation.

title: Bayesian-Optimized Superpixel-GrabCut for Traceable Optic Disc Segmentation
abstract: Optic disc (OD) segmentation is essential for diagnosing ophthalmic pathologies from retinal fundus images. However, prevailing deep learning approaches operate as opaque black boxes, lacking the inference-stage mathematical traceability--a critical requirement for algorithmic auditing and failure analysis in clinical workflows. This paper presents a fully algorithmically traceable and trainable segmentation pipeline that jointly combines superpixel decomposition, hybrid brightness-proximity superpixel scoring, morphological regularization, iterative GrabCut refinement, and elliptical shape fitting. The hyperparameter optimization is formulated as an objective function and solved via Bayesian optimization to eliminate manual parameter tuning. A quantitative evaluation on the Drishti-GS dataset demonstrates that our method achieves a Dice coefficient of 0.9536, matching state-of-the-art performance. By maintaining explicit mathematical transparency across all processing stages, our framework offers a deterministic, traceable alternative to black-box architectures for medical review and debugging.

title: The Role of Network Topology and Opponent Information in Shaping Cooperation in Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Systems
abstract: Several works have investigated the influence of graph topology on cooperation among artificial agents, while the majority of the literature has focused on modelling agents' adaptation through strategy imitation, which relies solely on the cumulative payoffs of others. This paper investigates scenarios in which each agent learns to play the two-player Iterated Prisoner's Dilemma (IPD) using deep reinforcement learning. Each agent is represented as a node in a graph, where its neighbours constitute the pool of opponents with whom it can interact. During each IPD episode, agents are provided with different types of information about their opponent, consisting of action history and opponent identity. Experimental results across different graph topologies show that the number of neighbours per node and the average path length are the main factors affecting the emergence of cooperation. We also show that, while partner selection fosters mutual cooperation by limiting the diversity of the opponent pool, providing agents with the identity of their opponent hinders the proliferation of cooperative strategies.

title: Intrinsic volumes of the quantum state space and mutually unbiased bases
abstract: Abstract Previous studies on the geometrical properties of the state space of a finite-level quantum system have determined its volume and surface area. Building on this foundation, we derive explicit formulas for two additional intrinsic volume quantities. The question of whether a complete set of mutually unbiased bases exists in dimension d can be equivalently framed as whether a specific convex polytope can be inscribed within the state space of a d -level quantum system. One motivation for our work was the hypothesis that a smaller intrinsic volume of the state space compared to the corresponding intrinsic volume of the mentioned polytope could rule out such an inscription. While our computations of these two intrinsic volumes do not lead to this conclusion, they nonetheless provide fundamental insights into the geometric structure of quantum state spaces. In particular, we show that these quantities can be used to rule out the existence of some unit-vector “configurations” (though not the one formed by the bases vectors of a complete set of mutually unbiased bases).

title: Modelling Uncertainty in Ontology for The Semantic Web Using Vague Graph Theory
abstract: Ontology is viewed as an explicit representation of conceptualization. It consists of a set of concepts, their definitions and their interrelationships. Ontologies are used to unambiguously model an area of knowledge by “semantically” defining the concepts and their relationships in a given domain in a way that can be understood by both humans and machines. One of the major limitations of traditional ontology formalism is its lack of support for the representation of uncertainty and imprecision. As a result, they cannot handle incomplete or partial knowledge. Attempts have been made by other researchers to address this problem using algebraic methods, such as rough sets, soft sets, fuzzy sets, and probabilistic approaches. However, the conceptualization of the proposed solutions in those approaches is not always the same as how ontologies are actually implemented. Ontology languages [such as Resource Description Framework (RDF), RDF Schema (RDFS), and Web Ontology Language (OWL)] are used for expressing ontologies for Semantic Web (SW) in a crisp manner. This paper proposed a vague graph approach to formalize uncertainty in ontology for the SW. The paper extended RDFvg and RDFSvg, respectively, where both syntactic and semantic extensions of the languages are proposed. Similarly, a description of vague OWL was provided as OWLvg.

title: Does AI strengthen business leadership decision making: literature review
abstract: Purpose - Examining how the interaction between Artificial Intelligence (AI) capabilities and organizational leadership dynamics can strengthen business strategic decision-making processes. Design/methodology/approach – A Systematic Literature Review (SLR) methodology following the PRISMA protocol was employed. Data were screened from the Scopus database up to July 2026, resulting in a final cohort of 30 English-language scholarly journal articles for qualitative analysis. Originality - Introducing the concept of "Algorithmic Bounded Rationality" to explain AI limitations (such as data bias, contextual rigidity, and factual inaccuracies) and developing a "Triple Helix" model that emphasizes the importance of synergy between machine precision and human cognitive curation (human-in-the-loop governance). Findings and Discussion – The effectiveness of AI is not technologically deterministic; AI capabilities—ranging from predictive analytics to generative models—require organizational mediators such as ethical leadership, a digital mindset, and strategic ambidexterity. AI acts as a cognitive prosthesis that frees up a leader's capacity from routine operational tasks, yet it still requires the contextual intuition and ethical governance of human leaders. Most literature focuses on quantitative or conceptual approaches, while in-depth, case-study-based qualitative research remains very limited. Conclusion – AI does not replace the role of executive leaders; instead, it serves as a cognitive aid. Organizations that successfully integrate AI's computational precision with ethical and responsive human leadership achieve the greatest competitive advantage. Keywords – Artificial Intelligence, Leadership Decision Making, Dynamic Managerial Capabilities, Algorithmic Bounded Rationality, Human AI Complementarity

title: The AI Persona Economy: Twelve Behavioral Archetypes Shaping the Future of AI Adoption
abstract: Ask ten people whether they “use AI” and the yes-or-no answer tells you almost nothing. One treats a chatbot as a faster search engine. Another lets it draft half of the working day. A third talks to it at midnight about things they tell no one else. A fourth signs the company’s entire AI budget while barely typing a prompt, and a fifth refuses the technology on principle. This paper argues that the question that now matters is not whether people use AI but what they are willing to trust it to do, and it offers a map: twelve types of AI user, from the Builder to the Churned Sceptic, organized into three tiers and described along six measurable dimensions. Three findings shape the map. People fall into stable AI habits remarkably fast, so the type someone becomes is partly created by product design, not just by personality. The types run on two separate logics, how much work is handed over and how close the relationship is allowed to get, and each carries its own distinct risk: costly errors on one side, dependency on the other. And each type should be visible in the clock: published data already shows sleep advice peaking at 5 a.m. and recipe requests at 6 p.m., so the map can be tested against the rhythms of an ordinary day. For AI leaders the consequences are direct: user counts conceal twelve different customers, and onboarding quietly decides which type each new user becomes. The paper closes with nine testable predictions, seven lessons for AI leadership, and a plan for putting the map on trial.

title: Sentinel-Augmented Reinforcement Learning with One-Step Ahead Predictive Safety Filtering
abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) consists of a general trial-and-error learning structure in which an agent, based on observations, receives rewards or punishments according to the action taken. This approach has proven to be efficient in many fields of application, such as video games, board games and even autonomous vehicles. But it is precisely in sensitive application areas, such as autonomous vehicles or other applications that require a high safety margin and need to eliminate errors, that the study of sentinel-assisted reinforcement learning was applied. It acts as a multi-agent reinforcement learning system with two collaborating agents. The first is the sentinel agent (teacher) that explores first, evaluates outcomes, and produces advice signals (positive / neutral / negative) to the main agent. The second one is the main agent (student) that receives these signals and adjusts its policy faster, minimizing trial and error. title: Quantum Entanglement-Driven Distributed Computing Architecture
abstract: This paper proposes a novel distributed computing architecture driven by quantum entanglement, aiming to overcome the limitations of traditional distributed computing methods. The core concept involves leveraging quantum entanglement for direct information transfer between computing nodes, eliminating the latency inherent in classical communication networks. This architecture utilizes a constructed quantum entanglement network to decompose computational tasks and accelerate processing through instantaneous node-to-node information exchange. The theoretical framework presented here outlines the key components and operational principles of this system, focusing on the potential to enable massively parallel computing and achieve significant speedups for complex calculations. The design prioritizes robust entanglement distribution and efficient task allocation, addressing key challenges in realizing this paradigm. The architecture's success hinges on the reliable generation and maintenance of entanglement across a distributed network, a critical factor for achieving the desired computational performance. Further research will focus on practical implementations and exploring the scalability of this approach.

title: Bio-Inspired Algorithms for Complex Network Optimization
abstract: This paper explores the application of bio-inspired algorithms to the optimization of complex networks. Traditional network optimization techniques often rely heavily on mathematical models, which can struggle to capture the inherent complexities and emergent behaviors found in real-world networks. This work proposes leveraging the principles of biological systems, specifically mimicking behaviors observed in ant colonies and fish schools, to drive network optimization. The core idea involves formulating network optimization problems as search tasks within these biological contexts. Algorithms such as the Ant Colony Optimization (ACO) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) are adapted and applied to problems involving network structure and performance, aiming to enhance efficiency and robustness. The paper details the underlying mechanisms, highlighting the advantages of this approach and its potential for addressing challenging network design and management scenarios. The core claim of this research is centered on utilizing bio-inspired algorithms to optimize complex networks. The core mechanism focuses on simulating biological behaviors to guide network optimization, ultimately improving network efficiency and robustness. ---

title: Quantum Multi-Variate Polarity Diversity Theorem Generalization in Higher-Dimensional Quantum States
abstract: This paper investigates the generalization of the multi-variate polarity diversity theorem to higher-dimensional quantum state spaces. We introduce a novel multi-variate polarity measure designed to capture the complexity of quantum states within these spaces, leveraging quantum entanglement and the inherent diversity of the state. The core of our work focuses on quantifying the relationship between this new polarity measure and key aspects of quantum information theory, including quantum information encoding schemes and quantum communication protocols. We demonstrate that this generalization provides a more robust framework for analyzing quantum states and their capacity for information processing. The results contribute to a deeper understanding of the fundamental properties governing quantum information and offer potential advancements in the design of efficient quantum algorithms and secure quantum communication systems. Specifically, we present a generalized theorem that allows for the identification of states with maximal diversity across multiple variables, a crucial factor in optimizing quantum information transmission and storage. Furthermore, we explore the implications of this theorem for the construction of novel quantum codes and protocols.

title: Title: Non-Linear Quantum State Collapse – Adaptive Quantum Error Correction
abstract: Quantum error correction is a critical component of future quantum computing, enabling the reliable transmission and manipulation of quantum information. Current error correction schemes rely on simplifying the quantum state, which inherently limits the achievable error correction rate. This paper explores the potential of non-linear quantum state collapse as a novel approach to improve error correction, proposing a dynamically adjusting collapse criterion to optimize error detection and correction. We present a preliminary design of this 'dynamic collapse' algorithm, detailing its operational principles and demonstrating its potential for significantly enhancing error correction efficiency. The core claim centers on achieving higher error correction rates through the exploitation of this adaptive mechanism. This work addresses a significant challenge in quantum information theory by offering a fundamentally new approach to error correction.

title: Fractal Tensor Decomposition for Anomaly Detection
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to anomaly detection based on fractal tensor decomposition. The core idea is that anomalous data points frequently exhibit fractal characteristics within high-dimensional tensor spaces. We propose a method that directly estimates the fractal dimension of tensor representations of data using techniques like box-counting. A loss function is then formulated to penalize deviations from a target fractal dimension, effectively isolating anomalies. The method leverages the inherent ability of tensors to capture complex, non-linear relationships within data, making them suitable for identifying subtle fractal patterns indicative of anomalous behavior. Experimental results (simulated data) demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach in distinguishing between normal and anomalous data points. The key contribution lies in applying fractal analysis, traditionally employed in image processing, to tensor data, offering a new perspective on anomaly detection.

title: Quantum Entanglement Probability Optimization
abstract: This paper investigates the use of quantum entanglement probability as a novel optimization technique for quantum computing. Traditional quantum algorithm design relies heavily on classical optimization methods, often limited by computational constraints. We introduce a new framework, leveraging the inherent probabilistic nature of quantum entanglement, to dynamically adjust quantum parameters, potentially enhancing both efficiency and precision. The core mechanism involves constructing a probabilistic model of quantum circuit parameters, where entanglement properties are integrated to guide parameter selection. This approach offers a potentially transformative path toward optimizing quantum computation, addressing limitations of existing algorithms and opening new avenues for exploration in quantum information processing. The paper demonstrates preliminary results through a simplified quantum circuit optimization scenario.

title: Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning with Abstract State Representation Learning
abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) frequently encounters challenges when dealing with complex environments characterized by high-dimensional state spaces. This paper proposes a novel hierarchical reinforcement learning (HRL) framework that addresses this limitation by incorporating abstract state representation learning. The core idea is to learn hierarchical representations of the environment, progressively moving from low-level sensory input to high-level strategic goals. This is achieved through an architecture where each level employs autoencoders or variational autoencoders to learn compressed, abstract representations. The framework aims to significantly improve learning efficiency and generalization capabilities in complex RL tasks. We argue that the multi-level abstraction approach enables more effective exploration and allows the agent to focus on relevant aspects of the environment, ultimately leading to faster convergence and better performance compared to traditional, single-level RL methods. This work contributes a practical and scalable approach to tackling complex RL problems.

title: RLG-TPV: Radar- and LiDAR-Guided Tri-Perspective View Fusion for Camera-Radar 3D Object Detection
abstract: Tri-Perspective View (TPV) representations describe 3D scene structure through top, side, and front feature planes, but existing TPV lifting is primarily camera-based, leaving the depth of sampled image evidence ambiguous along projected camera rays. We propose RLG-TPV, a multimodal TPV framework for camera-radar 3D object detection in which radar and training-time LiDAR provide complementary geometric guidance during representation construction. A ray-guided deformable-attention lift weights sampled image features using LiDAR-supervised camera depth probabilities and radar frustum occupancy, while radar additionally refines the depth distribution before lifting. Because conventional radar provides limited elevation information, LiDAR-derived class-occupancy targets supervise the side and front planes during training; the corresponding heads are removed at inference, so deployment requires only cameras and radar. For temporal aggregation, Doppler-guided temporal fusion aligns past features using a motion field anchored by measured radar radial velocity, with gating that limits warping in regions without supported motion. An RCS-aware radar scatter further allows radar evidence to spread over spatial neighborhoods conditioned on radar cross section. On the nuScenes validation set, RLG-TPV achieves 0.4981 mAP and 0.5959 NDS, reducing orientation and velocity error by 31.9\% and 30.7\% relative to the published CRN baseline. Ablation studies show that ray-level geometric guidance is a major contributor to the final performance.

title: From Analytics to Tumor Boards: An Evidence-Linked Multi-Agent Workflow for Oncology Feature Extraction
abstract: Clinically relevant oncology information is distributed across heterogeneous, longitudinal documentation, creating substantial abstraction burden and requiring accurate attribution across specimens, tumors, biomarkers, and time points, while manual cancer-registry abstraction can require 27.2 minutes per case, highlighting the need for scalable methods that preserve clinical context while converting documentation into structured data. We evaluate an oncology information-extraction workflow in which OncoLens supplies multi-source, oncology-aware document selection, aggregation, and normalization from integrated EHRs, while the NimbleMind Multi-Agent System (nMAS) is a configurable oncology information-extraction workflow that extracts clinically relevant structured fields from fragmented oncology documentation. The extraction task uses a clinician-informed schema of 328 attributes spanning report metadata, diagnosis, staging, and cancer-type-specific information. nMAS separates clinician-defined field specifications from model execution and combines complexity-aware extraction, report-level consolidation, and source-grounded validation. The retrospective evaluation included 230 de-identified oncology documents from 40 patients and 418 clinician-reviewed document-field pairs containing 1,126 non-empty reference values. Evaluation focused on fields identified by clinicians as present in the source documents rather than exhaustively annotating all 328 schema fields. nMAS achieved a rank-weighted value-level precision of 82.6%, recall of 87.5%, and F1 of 85.0%, compared with an F1 of 66.4% for an independently implemented UMA-style MiniMax M2.5 comparator. These findings support the feasibility of using a configurable, source-grounded extraction workflow to convert fragmented oncology documentation into reusable structured data.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Bayesian Optimization for Hyperparameter Tuning
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of quantum computing to accelerate hyperparameter tuning within Bayesian optimization frameworks. Traditional Bayesian optimization can be computationally expensive, particularly when dealing with high-dimensional hyperparameter spaces. We propose a novel approach leveraging quantum amplitude estimation (QAE) to efficiently estimate the expected improvement function, a core component of Bayesian optimization. The theoretical framework outlines how QAE's speedup can translate into faster convergence and improved hyperparameter selection. We present a detailed mathematical description of the algorithm and its key components, emphasizing the transformation of the Bayesian optimization problem into a suitable form for quantum execution. The primary focus is on the theoretical advantages, without experimental validation, exploring the potential for significant speedups compared to classical Bayesian optimization methods. The paper concludes with a discussion of the challenges and future directions for this research area.

title: Based on Bio-Inspired Genetic Algorithms for Program Optimization
abstract: This paper explores the application of bio-inspired genetic algorithms, specifically a neural network-based genetic algorithm, for program optimization. Traditional optimization methods often struggle with the complex and dynamic nature of software, leading to suboptimal performance and resource utilization. This research proposes a novel approach where programs are treated as genetic units, subjected to evolutionary processes such as mutation, crossover, and selection, guided by a neural network that mimics the functionality of biological neurons to refine the optimization process. The core claim is that this hybrid approach – combining the strengths of genetic algorithms with the learning capabilities of neural networks – can significantly enhance program optimization effectiveness. The methodology details the construction of the genetic algorithm with a neural network component, focusing on the encoding of program structures and the design of the neural network's objective function. The potential benefits of this methodology, including improved performance and resource efficiency, are discussed.

title: Neuro-Symbolic Grounding of Embodied Agents in Simulated Environments
abstract: This paper investigates the challenge of translating symbolic instructions into physical actions for embodied agents, a fundamental problem in artificial intelligence and robotics. The core claim is that existing approaches often fail to adequately bridge the gap between symbolic reasoning and the complexities of physical interaction. This work proposes a novel neuro-symbolic grounding technique designed to address this limitation. The technique leverages the strengths of both neural networks (for perception and adaptation) and symbolic reasoning (for structured instruction following) within a simulated environment. title: Quantum Computation Based on Neuronal Dynamics
abstract: This paper proposes a novel quantum computing model that leverages the dynamics of neuronal behavior as its foundational building blocks. Unlike conventional quantum computing approaches reliant on purely classical qubits, this model utilizes quantum systems designed to mimic the dynamic changes observed in biological neural networks, specifically at the level of synaptic connections. The core principle involves employing quantum superposition and interference to construct quantum bits (qubits) representing the state of these simulated synapses. Algorithm execution is achieved through precise manipulation, or "quantum tuning," of these qubits. The proposed architecture represents a biologically-inspired paradigm shift in quantum computation, potentially offering advantages in terms of computational efficiency and resilience, particularly for problems exhibiting inherent biological complexity. This work outlines the theoretical framework, key equations, and the fundamental principles driving this new approach to quantum information processing.

title: Neural Turing Machines with Multi-Modal Data Fusion
abstract: This paper proposes a novel architecture, the Neural Turing Machine with Multi-Modal Data Fusion (NTM-MMDF), designed to achieve general intelligence by integrating the computational power of neural networks with the control capabilities of Turing Machines and effectively fusing multi-modal data. The core idea is to leverage the inherent parallelism of neural networks for pattern recognition and representation learning, coupled with the sequential reasoning and memory access mechanisms of Turing Machines, to process complex inputs. Specifically, multi-modal data (e.g., images, text, audio) are used to drive the operation and decision-making process of the NTM. The system simulates neural network computations via the interaction of its neurons while utilizing the Turing Machine's ability to perform logical inference and control. The NTM-MMDF aims to overcome limitations of conventional neural networks by incorporating external memory and enabling more sophisticated data integration strategies. Mathematical formulations are presented to describe the key components and operational principles of the NTM-MMDF. The architecture demonstrates potential for applications requiring robust understanding and reasoning across diverse data types, paving the way for more adaptable and intelligent systems.

title: Based on Quantum Mechanics Principles Hardware Accelerator Design
abstract: This paper presents the design of a novel hardware accelerator leveraging fundamental principles of quantum mechanics. The core concept involves translating specific computational algorithms into quantum circuits and executing them on quantum hardware platforms such as superconducting qubits or ion traps. This approach aims to achieve significant speedup compared to classical algorithms. The design focuses on optimizing the quantum circuit for targeted algorithms, considering factors like qubit connectivity, gate fidelity, and measurement schemes. This work outlines the theoretical framework, key design considerations, and potential performance gains anticipated from utilizing quantum mechanical phenomena like superposition and entanglement for hardware acceleration. The primary goal is to demonstrate the feasibility and potential of quantum-inspired hardware accelerators for solving computationally intensive problems. ---

title: Dynamic Topology Program Synthesis
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to program synthesis, termed Dynamic Topology Program Synthesis (DTPyS), which addresses the limitations of traditional static program synthesis techniques. The core idea is to automatically generate program code that adapts to the evolving topology of complex software systems. We leverage reinforcement learning (RL) as the central mechanism, training a program synthesizer to learn the generation of appropriate communication protocols and data routing algorithms based on observed changes in the system's topology. Unlike existing methods that primarily operate on static topologies, DTPyS enables the synthesis of programs that can dynamically respond to and integrate with systems exhibiting temporal and structural variation. The system learns through trial and error, optimizing its synthesis strategy based on feedback from the target system. This research contributes to a paradigm shift in program synthesis, moving beyond static representations towards truly adaptive and dynamic software development. The proposed approach offers the potential to significantly reduce development time and improve the robustness of software systems operating in unpredictable environments.

title: Algorithmic Reservoir for Spatio-Temporal Data
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to reservoir computing, termed the "algorithmic reservoir," specifically designed to address the complexities of spatio-temporal data. The core claim is that a strategically engineered recurrent neural network, acting as a dedicated reservoir, can significantly enhance the efficiency and effectiveness of learning from data exhibiting inherent spatio-temporal correlations. The proposed mechanism utilizes a recurrent neural network architecture meticulously crafted to capture both spatial and temporal dependencies concurrently. We argue that this focused approach, diverging from general-purpose reservoir designs, offers the potential to outperform conventional methods in scenarios involving spatio-temporal data analysis and prediction. The paper details the architectural considerations and key operational principles of this algorithmic reservoir, emphasizing its potential applications across diverse fields.

title: Quantum Error Correction Based on Time Streams
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to quantum error correction by leveraging the concept of time streams. Traditional quantum error correction methods primarily focus on correcting errors directly within the quantum states of qubits. This work introduces a fundamentally different perspective, treating the quantum state of a qubit as a time series and utilizing time series analysis techniques for error detection and correction. Specifically, we employ time series prediction models to identify anomalies within the time series data, effectively pinpointing the occurrence of errors. The core of this method lies in recognizing that the evolution of a qubit's state over time, represented as a time series, inherently contains information about the underlying errors. This approach offers a potentially more robust and efficient method for quantum error correction, particularly in scenarios where the dynamics of qubit evolution are complex and difficult to model directly. The paper outlines the theoretical framework and proposes a methodology for implementing this approach, highlighting its potential advantages and future research directions.

title: 基于量子纠缠的算术几何的非欧性分析
abstract: This paper explores the potential of quantum entanglement to revolutionize the field of numerical geometry, specifically focusing on the analysis of non-Euclidean geometry. We propose a novel approach that leverages quantum entanglement to detect and quantify the non-Euclidean nature of geometric structures. Through a carefully constructed mathematical framework, we demonstrate the potential of this method to enhance the accuracy and efficiency of numerical geometric computations, offering a fundamentally different perspective on geometric properties. The core mechanism involves identifying and exploiting the correlations inherent in entangled states to reveal subtle geometric anomalies that are difficult to detect with traditional methods. The resulting analysis provides a pathway towards a more robust and efficient approach to geometric modeling and computation.
