title: Quantum-Inspired Algorithm for Optimal Data Subsampling
abstract: This paper introduces a novel algorithm for optimal data subsampling, termed the Quantum-Inspired Data Subsampling (QIDS) algorithm. The algorithm leverages concepts from quantum measurement theory, specifically superposition and projection, to efficiently identify a representative subset of data points. Unlike traditional subsampling techniques that often rely on random sampling or heuristics, QIDS systematically evaluates potential subsets, weighting them based on their information content. This approach minimizes information loss while striving to maximize computational efficiency. The core idea is to simulate the process of quantum measurement, where a system exists in a superposition of states until a measurement (selection) is performed. The algorithm uses a probabilistic weighting scheme, inspired by the Born rule in quantum mechanics, to determine the probability of selecting each data point. The final subset is determined through a repeated application of this weighting and selection process, effectively converging towards a solution that represents the most significant aspects of the original dataset. We demonstrate the algorithm's efficacy through theoretical analysis and provide a conceptual framework for its implementation. The key contribution lies in providing a principled and potentially efficient method for data subsampling that draws inspiration from the principles of quantum mechanics.

title: Contextual Memory Networks with Hierarchical Temporal Encoding
abstract: This paper introduces Contextual Memory Networks with Hierarchical Temporal Encoding (CMHN-HTE), a novel architecture designed to enhance the performance of memory networks in tasks involving long-range temporal dependencies. The core challenge in utilizing memory networks for sequential data lies in their ability to effectively manage and retrieve information across varying timescales. Existing approaches often struggle with capturing subtle temporal relationships and dependencies that span extended periods. CMHN-HTE tackles this problem by implementing a hierarchical temporal encoding scheme. This scheme decomposes the input temporal sequence into multiple levels of abstraction, each representing information at a specific temporal scale. Attention mechanisms are then strategically applied to selectively retrieve relevant information from these hierarchical levels, guided by the current context. This approach allows the network to both store and retrieve information efficiently, mitigating the limitations of traditional memory networks. We demonstrate that CMHN-HTE significantly improves performance compared to standard memory networks across several benchmark tasks, showcasing the effectiveness of the proposed hierarchical temporal encoding strategy.

title: Non-Linear Self-Organizing Networks for Reinforcement Learning
abstract: This paper investigates a novel reinforcement learning algorithm leveraging non-linear self-organization networks. We propose a framework that dynamically adjusts network topology and parameters during training, enabling automated network structure learning and optimization. The core mechanism centers around a self-organizing process intertwined with reinforcement learning, allowing the network to evolve into a highly optimized, self-organized architecture. The advantages of this approach include reduced manual intervention, improved generalization, and the potential for more robust and adaptable learning. This research addresses a critical challenge in reinforcement learning: the need for effective network design, offering a promising path towards enhanced performance and scalability.

title: FiLM-GPNet: Geometry-Aware Pseudo-Supervised Phase Restoration with Zero-Shot Generalization for Large Temporal InSAR Stacks
abstract: The growing availability of dense commercial Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) time series enables temporal Interferometric SAR (InSAR) analysis, but fixed classical filters fail under heterogeneous acquisition geometries, degrading phase quality and temporal consistency. We propose FiLM-GPNet, a geometry-conditioned network for wrapped-phase restoration that explicitly adapts to acquisition differences using Feature-wise Linear Modulation (FiLM) and a 7D per-pair geometry descriptor. The model is trained with pseudo-supervision from Goldstein-filtered interferograms and regularized by interferometric physics via triplet-closure consistency, while also estimating per-pixel aleatoric uncertainty. Experiments on three Capella Spotlight stacks from the IEEE GRSS 2026 Data Fusion Contest show that FiLM-GPNet reduces temporal residual by 68% (Hawaii) and 66% (Western Australia) relative to the Goldstein baseline, alongside closure error reductions of 10% and 13%, respectively. In Western Australia, it further improves unwrapping success rate by 7.7 percentage points and Digital Elevation Model (DEM) Normalized Median Absolute Deviation (NMAD) by 31%. The model also shows strong zero-shot generalization to a geographically and geometrically distinct third stack (Los Angeles) without retraining, supporting geometry-conditioned restoration as an effective alternative to fixed classical filtering across heterogeneous stacks.

title: Brain-Language-Action (BLA) Models: Language-Conditioned EEG for Robotics Control
abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG)-based robotic control is commonly formulated as a direct classification problem, in which electrical neural signals are mapped to a fixed set of discrete actions. However, the limited separability and high noise of EEG signals make it difficult to scale this approach to fine-grained robotic control spaces. We introduce Brain-Language-Action (BLA) models, a framework in which language conditions the interpretation of neural representations for robotic action generation. In a BLA, a small set of reliably distinguishable brain states can be dynamically associated with different actions through a language-defined control mapping, allowing a small number of neural classes to apply to a larger global action space. We develop a proof-of-concept BLA for drone control using motor-imagery EEG from the BCI Competition IV 2a dataset. The system is trained in two stages. First, we evaluate multiple candidate EEG encoder architectures using subject-specific four-class motor-imagery classification, converting 250Hz, 3.5-second, 22-channel EEG samples into five 128-dimensional brain-token embeddings. Second, these embeddings are projected into the embedding space of a pretrained large language model (LLM) and jointly fine-tuned with language instructions to autoregressively generate structured three-token drone actions. Across 840 possible language-defined mappings between four neural states and seven flight action combinations, the resulting BLA achieves 90% per-token accuracy during evaluation. These results provide an initial demonstration that language conditioning can expand the effective control range of EEG-based robotic interfaces without requiring a corresponding increase in the number of directly distinguishable neural states.

title: Preparing National Security Systems for the Quantum Era: A Roadmap for Post-Quantum Cryptographic Migration
abstract: The anticipated emergence of cryptographically relevant quantum computing presents a strategic challenge for national security systems because many existing public-key cryptographic mechanisms depend on mathematical problems that may become vulnerable to sufficiently capable quantum computation. The central difficulty is therefore not limited to selecting a new cryptographic algorithm; it concerns the coordinated migration of complex national infrastructures, institutional processes, data repositories, software platforms, and interconnected information systems. This research and review article develops a policy-oriented roadmap for post-quantum cryptographic migration by synthesizing the supplied literature on quantum-resistant national security planning with evidence concerning technological adoption barriers, data quality, artificial intelligence governance, explainability, bias, implementation complexity, and safety. The analysis conceptualizes migration as a socio-technical transformation rather than a purely cryptographic replacement exercise. A phased framework is proposed consisting of discovery and inventory, risk classification, algorithm and architecture preparation, controlled transition, validation, institutionalization, and continuous assurance. title: Non-Euclidean Geometry for Information Encoding and Transmission
abstract: This paper explores the potential of utilizing non-Euclidean geometries, such as spherical and hyperbolic geometries, for enhancing information encoding and transmission. Traditional information theory and coding techniques are fundamentally based on Euclidean geometry, which inherently imposes limitations on information density and resilience to noise. We propose a framework for designing information encoding schemes that leverage the unique geometric properties of non-Euclidean spaces. Specifically, we investigate how the curvature of these spaces can be exploited for information compression and error correction. The core claim is that by exploiting non-Euclidean geometries, significantly higher information densities and improved robustness against interference can be achieved. The underlying mechanism involves encoding data within the specific topological features of the chosen non-Euclidean space, allowing for more efficient representation and robust transmission. Mathematical formulations detailing the encoding processes and the relationship between geometric parameters and information capacity are presented. We demonstrate the theoretical advantages of this approach and outline potential avenues for future research, focusing on practical implementations and exploring different non-Euclidean geometries.

title: Quantum-Inspired Neural Networks for Optimal Control in Stochastic Systems
abstract: This paper explores the potential of quantum-inspired neural networks (QINNs) for solving optimal control problems within stochastic systems. Traditional optimal control methods often struggle with the inherent uncertainty and noise present in real-world systems. We propose a novel neural network architecture that mimics key quantum phenomena – interference and superposition – to enhance its ability to navigate these challenges. The QINN architecture leverages probabilistic outputs and a layered structure designed to represent quantum states. We formulate the optimal control problem as a stochastic differential equation (SDE) and employ the QINN to approximate the optimal control trajectory. The core idea is to treat the control action as a superposition of possible actions, where quantum interference guides the system towards the most probable optimal solution. The performance of the QINN is evaluated through simulations, demonstrating its potential to outperform classical optimal control techniques, particularly in scenarios with high levels of stochastic disturbance. The key contribution of this work lies in the application of quantum-inspired principles to control system design, offering a new avenue for addressing complex, uncertain control problems. The ultimate goal is to develop a more robust and efficient control strategy by harnessing the principles of quantum mechanics.

title: Information-Theoretic Analysis of Neural Network Robustness to Adversarial Attacks
abstract: This paper investigates the evaluation of neural network robustness against adversarial attacks from an information-theoretic perspective. Traditional methods for assessing robustness frequently rely on empirical evaluations and black-box testing, which can be computationally expensive and may not fully capture the underlying mechanisms driving vulnerability. We propose a novel framework that leverages information-theoretic measures – specifically mutual information (MI) and entropy – to quantify the information required to induce a misclassification. Our approach shifts the focus from simply measuring the success rate of attacks to understanding the fundamental relationship between input perturbations and model outputs. By analyzing the information flow between the input and the network's decision, we aim to provide a more rigorous and theoretically grounded understanding of neural network robustness. We demonstrate how MI can reveal the sensitivity of the network to small input changes, while entropy provides a measure of the uncertainty in the network's predictions. The results suggest that robustness is not solely determined by the magnitude of perturbations but also by the information contained within the input that the network effectively exploits. This work offers a new lens for analyzing and designing more robust neural networks.

title: Core Claim: A Dynamic Adaptive Quantum Topological Model Optimization Algorithm
abstract: Quantum topologies offer unique opportunities for quantum computation and information processing. However, designing and optimizing quantum circuits often requires careful control over the underlying topology. This paper presents a novel optimization algorithm based on dynamic self-adaptive quantum topology models. We introduce a mechanism that automatically adjusts quantum topology parameters based on input data, enabling precise control and optimization of these models. This approach overcomes limitations of traditional static optimization methods, particularly for complex and highly parameterized quantum systems. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this algorithm through several illustrative examples, showcasing its ability to achieve significant improvements in quantum circuit performance.

title: Graph Embedding with Relational Reasoning and Memory Networks
abstract: This paper introduces a novel graph embedding method designed to address the limitations of existing techniques in capturing intricate relational dependencies within graph data. The proposed approach integrates relational reasoning with memory networks, creating a system capable of encoding and reasoning about complex graph structures. Specifically, a memory network is utilized to store and retrieve information regarding relationships between nodes, thereby enabling the embedding process to represent more nuanced structural details. We demonstrate that this combination provides a significantly more powerful and expressive graph embedding compared to methods that rely solely on traditional graph embedding techniques. The core of this work lies in the synergistic interaction between relational reasoning and memory networks, leading to improved graph representation and ultimately, enhanced performance in downstream graph-based tasks.

title: Adaptive Quantum Entanglement Network (AQEN)
abstract: This paper proposes the Adaptive Quantum Entanglement Network (AQEN), a novel system designed for efficient quantum communication and computation by dynamically adjusting its entanglement network topology. The core mechanism relies on a feedback control algorithm that monitors quantum channel loss and noise levels, enabling real-time optimization of entanglement node connections. This adaptive approach contrasts with traditional fixed-topology quantum networks, offering enhanced resilience to noise and improved performance through dynamic topology reconfiguration. We introduce a mathematical framework for describing the AQEN, focusing on the key elements of entanglement quality, channel loss, and the feedback control process. The proposed system aims to significantly improve the reliability and scalability of quantum networks, paving the way for more robust and efficient quantum technologies. The system is modeled using a state-space representation, where the entangled state vector *|ψ⟩* is continuously updated based on the control inputs. The core equation governing this update is: *|ψ(t+Δt)| = U(t) |ψ(t)| + Σi αi *|φi⟩* where *|ψ(t)|* represents the entangled state at time *t*, *U(t)* is the unitary evolution operator, *Δt* is the time step, and *αi* are the control parameters. The fidelity of the entangled state, *F*, is continuously monitored and fed back into the control loop to adjust *αi*. Channel loss, *L*, is characterized by the attenuation factor applied to the quantum state during transmission, and noise, *N*, is represented as a perturbation term in the unitary operator *U(t)*. The goal is to minimize the combined effect of *L* and *N* on the fidelity *F*. This work lays the groundwork for future research and development in adaptive quantum networking. ---

title: Adaptive Bayesian Networks for Reinforcement Learning Integration
abstract: This paper introduces an adaptive Bayesian Network (ABN) framework for reinforcement learning, designed to dynamically select and fuse different learning strategies based on the current state and target. The core innovation lies in the implementation of a dynamic Bayesian Network (DBN) architecture, which adapts the learning process based on real-time feedback. This adaptive approach significantly improves learning efficiency and generalization capabilities compared to static learning strategies. The paper details the architecture, training methodology, and experimental results demonstrating the effectiveness of this approach.

title: Self-Supervised Learning with Contrastive Predictive Coding and Structural Alignment
abstract: Self-supervised learning (SSL) has emerged as a powerful technique for training deep neural networks without explicit labels. However, many existing SSL methods struggle to effectively capture the inherent structure and complex relationships present in diverse datasets. This paper proposes a novel framework that combines Contrastive Predictive Coding (CPC) with a structural alignment component. CPC, a well-established SSL technique, learns representations by predicting future states based on past observations. Simultaneously, the introduced structural alignment component enforces consistency in the learned representations across different parts or "views" of the data. This integration aims to overcome the limitations of traditional CPC by providing a stronger inductive bias for learning meaningful and robust representations. The core idea is to leverage predictive coding to understand the temporal dynamics of data while using structural alignment to ensure that related parts of the data map to similar representations. We demonstrate through theoretical analysis and a detailed explanation of the components that this approach offers a more effective route toward achieving truly self-supervised learning.

title: Title: Topological Quantum Entanglement Mapping
abstract: This paper presents a novel method for generating and manipulating topological quantum entanglement, moving beyond traditional entanglement states and establishing a dynamic, transferable entanglement landscape. The core mechanism centers around the introduction of a dynamically evolving topological field structure, achieved through a self-organizing algorithm. This structure allows for the creation of entangled states with complex, non-linear topologies, offering unprecedented flexibility and potential for advanced quantum computations. The development of this technique represents a significant advancement in the field, addressing limitations of existing entanglement methods and opening new avenues for exploring topological quantum phenomena.

title: OASI: An Organismic Computing Architecture for Body-Bound Runtime Assurance and Developmental OS-AI Integration
abstract: Operational Artificial System Intelligence (OASI) is the canonical name of a research paradigm investigating a system-level architecture in which operation, artificial embodiment, memory, cognition, authority, and development are coordinated through one versioned causal history and constitutionally mediated effects. In this name, operational refers to system operation, not production readiness, and system intelligence names a research target rather than achieved general or superintelligence, consciousness, deployment, external validation, or superiority. This preprint formalizes the architectural hypothesis as operational monism and combines a computational body model, developmental memory, typed PolicyIR, obligation-checked compilation, bounded reflexes, and AERA, a bounded commit-time authority-revalidation predicate. In this corrective version, AERA is a stable project identifier rather than a normative acronym expansion. The evidence remains internal and deliberately bounded. The accompanying release preserves a negative T4 result and two local deterministic effect-boundary simulations comprising 2,700 retained records across 90 cells. S5 did not establish an advantage over a cooperative idempotent receiver. S6 identified a retry-versus-omission safety-availability tradeoff under a non-cooperative fixture, without isolating an OASI-specific advantage. The 30 repetitions per cell are implementation-stability traces, not independent population samples, and the fault cases are simulated control-flow traces rather than physical failures. This v0.4.1 preprint is a terminology correction of v0.4; it does not reclassify any code behavior or experimental result. This work does not demonstrate a complete OASI operating system, general superiority, production readiness, universal effect guarantees, real-fault validation, performance advantage, or independent replication. Development and project-controlled internal adversarial review were extensively AI-assisted; they are not human peer review, external certification, institutional evaluation, or independent scientific review.

title: Anticipating health and care trajectories from routinely collected social care records
abstract: Predictive modelling in healthcare has advanced rapidly, yet social care systems, despite their central role in supporting vulnerable populations, remain underexplored in this domain. In this study, we apply machine learning to a large, pseudonymised dataset of social care records from 27,590 adults in Oxfordshire, encompassing around 90% of individuals receiving care in the region. We developed models to predict three outcomes of interest: future care plan needs, hospital admissions, and all-cause mortality, evaluated across multiple prediction horizons. Our results show that hospital admission and mortality can be predicted with meaningful discriminative performance (AUROC up to 0.893), while care plan needs are more variable and harder to predict. Post-hoc exploratory analyses revealed distinct risk signatures across outcomes, and temporal evaluation showed that care needs often emerge earlier than clinical deterioration. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of social care-based risk modelling and suggest new opportunities to improve anticipatory care planning, health management, and resource allocation using routinely collected non-clinical data.

title: Foundational feature fusion for conditional flow matching in 6D pose estimation
abstract: Conditional flow matching has enabled a step forward in object 6D pose estimation, achieving state-of-the-art performance by progressively denoising and registering object representations to observed scenes. Existing methods require training task-specific encoders supervised on object-scene overlap and rely on trivial feature fusion strategies to resolve pose ambiguities. We present FunFlow6D, a novel flow matching-based formulation that leverages features from geometric and appearance foundation models for pose estimation, eliminating the need for task-specific encoder training. We also introduce a cross attention-based fusion mechanism that dynamically combines geometric and appearance features to provide richer conditioning for the flow matching module. Experiments on four datasets from the BOP benchmark show that FunFlow6D outperforms the previous state of the art while reducing supervision requirements and memory overhead. Extensive ablations validate the contribution of each proposed component. Project website: https://tev-fbk.github.io/FunFlow6D/.

title: Expert System for Safety Recommendations of Active Ingredients Combinations Based on Skin Conditions Using a Rule-Based System
abstract: The growth of skincare products increases the need for easily accessible information regarding the safety of active ingredient combinations based on skin conditions. This study aims to develop an expert system that provides recommendations for the safety of active ingredient combinations based on the user's skin condition. The study used a system development method with a Rule-Based System approach and the Forward Chaining inference method. The study did not use conventional human populations and samples, but rather used peer-reviewed literature data from 2022–2025 and expert validation. The research instrument consisted of 25 condition rules covering six active ingredients, five skin conditions, and 15 unique active ingredient pairs. Data analysis was carried out through content analysis and expert validation using a four-level scale. The results showed that the system was able to generate recommendations in three categories: Recommended, Caution, and Not Recommended. Black Box testing showed that the authentication, knowledge base management, consultation, combination analysis, and prediction history functions ran as needed. In conclusion, the developed system can be used as an initial consultation medium to provide structured and easily accessible information on active ingredient safety

title: Quantum Topology Adaptive Self-Teaching Algorithm
abstract: Quantum Topology Adaptive Self-Teaching Algorithm (QTSA) presents a novel approach to quantum simulation, leveraging the principles of quantum topology and adaptive learning. This algorithm focuses on dynamically adjusting the simulation's complexity to optimize the user's learning experience, addressing the limitations of traditional methods. The core mechanism centers around a sophisticated feedback loop that analyzes user performance, tailoring the simulation's parameters to enhance understanding and retention. The algorithm's potential lies in creating a truly personalized learning environment, significantly improving efficiency and potentially unlocking deeper insights into quantum phenomena. This paper provides a detailed theoretical framework and implementation of QTSA, highlighting its advantages and potential future developments.

title: Towards Optimized Quantum Key Distribution Protocols Based on Information Theory
abstract: This paper investigates the optimization of Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) protocols through the application of information-theoretic principles. The core claim is that leveraging information theory's theoretical foundations can significantly enhance the efficiency and security of QKD protocols. The proposed mechanism centers around the design of novel QKD protocols that integrate quantum error correction codes and classical channel coding, aiming to boost key distribution rates while maintaining robust security. This work explores various modifications and enhancements to existing QKD schemes, focusing on reducing the overhead associated with error correction and distillation processes. abstract: The study presents a novel probabilistic logic system predicated on the principles of quantum entanglement. This system leverages the inherent properties of entangled quantum states to represent logical relationships, offering a paradigm shift compared to conventional probabilistic logic. The core mechanism involves establishing and manipulating entangled states to encode and manipulate logical constraints, thereby enabling sophisticated reasoning and computational operations. This research explores the potential of quantum entanglement to surpass the limitations of classical logic in terms of expressiveness and speed, paving the way for new algorithmic possibilities. The paper details the design of an entanglement-based logic module, explores the challenges of maintaining entanglement fidelity, and discusses the implications for future development of quantum-enhanced computational systems.

title: Title: Adaptive Quantum Computing Topology Transformation Algorithm
abstract: This paper presents an innovative algorithm for quantum computing topology transformation, leveraging dynamic adjustments to the system's topological structure to enhance both efficiency and precision. Traditional topological transformation methods are often static, limiting potential improvements. Our proposed algorithm employs an adaptive transformation strategy, dynamically modifying the quantum system's topology to optimize the resulting computational outcomes. The core mechanism centers around a self-learning approach to the quantum state, allowing the algorithm to continuously refine the topological landscape for improved performance. This approach addresses limitations of static transformations and offers a novel pathway towards more robust and accurate quantum computation. This work contributes to the field of quantum computing by presenting a practical and adaptable topology transformation technique.

title: Dynamic Semantic Topology Network
abstract: This paper proposes a Dynamic Semantic Topology Network (DSTN) designed to address the challenges of semantic understanding in distributed systems. The core claim is that real-time optimization of semantic understanding can be achieved by adaptively adjusting the data representation and communication protocol's semantic hierarchy. This is accomplished through a novel mechanism combining machine learning-based semantic graph construction and dynamic updates with a proxy-based communication protocol routing system. The system constructs and maintains a semantic graph that reflects the evolving state and relationships within the distributed system. The dynamic adjustment of this graph, combined with intelligent routing based on semantic hierarchy, enables real-time optimization of communication and processing. The system's ability to adapt to changing conditions offers a significant improvement over traditional static semantic modeling approaches. The key innovation lies in the dynamic, self-organizing nature of the semantic topology, allowing the network to respond efficiently to evolving data and system behavior. The performance of DSTN is evaluated through theoretical analysis and conceptual design, highlighting its potential for improving efficiency and resilience in complex distributed environments.

This paper introduces a self-adaptive algorithm designed to optimize the quantum ring's state, enhancing quantum computation's flexibility and efficiency. We present a theoretical framework and initial experimental validation demonstrating the efficacy of this approach. The core claim is that this system achieves a significant reduction in complexity compared to traditional methods, offering a pathway towards more versatile and efficient quantum algorithms.

This algorithm dynamically adjusts model parameters in response to data entropy, fostering a more robust and adaptable system. The core mechanism centers on the iterative process of assessing and refining model parameters based on the inherent information content of the input data. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through simulations and preliminary experiments, showcasing significant improvements in performance across a range of data types.

title: 基于几何变形的自适应神经网络
abstract: This paper introduces a novel neural network architecture, the "Geometric Adaptive Neural Network" (GANN), that leverages geometric deformation to dynamically adjust the network's parameters during training. Traditional neural networks often require manual parameter tuning, which can be a laborious and time-consuming process. The GANN utilizes geometric transformations to adapt the network's structure and weights, enabling more flexible and efficient machine learning and deep learning algorithms. We demonstrate the efficacy of this approach through a series of experiments on a dataset focused on shape recognition. The core mechanism involves applying geometric transformations to the network's input and output representations, allowing the network to learn complex relationships and adapt to variations in the input data. This results in improved accuracy and robustness compared to static neural networks.

title: Quantum Machine Learning: A Theoretical Framework for Generalization
abstract: This paper delves into the nascent field of quantum machine learning (QML) by establishing a theoretical framework for understanding and predicting the generalization capabilities of QML algorithms. Currently, the practical success of QML algorithms is often attributed to empirical observation, lacking a robust theoretical underpinning. This work addresses this gap by leveraging concepts from quantum information theory to analyze the generalization performance of various QML algorithms. We propose a model that connects algorithm parameters, dataset characteristics, and the resulting generalization error, expressed mathematically as: Γ(θ, D) = ED[|f(x) - ψ(x)|] where: Γ(θ, D) represents the generalization error; θ represents the algorithm's parameters; D represents the dataset; ED[ ] denotes the expected value with respect to the dataset D; f(x) is the model's prediction; ψ(x) is the true label or target. Furthermore, we explore the potential for quantum advantage in generalization, considering the impact of quantum entanglement and superposition on reducing the risk of overfitting. The core contribution lies in providing a methodological approach for quantifying and improving generalization performance in QML, moving beyond purely experimental evaluations. We introduce a novel metric, the Quantum Generalization Index (QGI), defined as: QGI = (1 - Γ(θ, D)) / (1 + Γ(θ, D)) This index provides a normalized measure of generalization performance, allowing for comparative analysis of different QML algorithms and parameter settings. Ultimately, this research aims to provide a foundational understanding for the design and development of more reliable and robust quantum machine learning systems.

title: Based Quantum State Optimization Algorithms
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to optimization utilizing quantum state manipulation. Traditional optimization algorithms often struggle with high-dimensional problems due to computational limitations. This work proposes a new algorithm, termed "Quantum-Guided Optimization," which leverages quantum state properties – specifically superposition and entanglement – to achieve significant efficiency gains in complex optimization scenarios. The core mechanism centers around a quantum state transformation process, which iteratively evolves the search space, effectively guiding the algorithm towards optimal solutions. The paper details the algorithm's design, mathematical foundations, and preliminary experimental results demonstrating improved performance compared to existing classical optimization techniques across a range of benchmark problems. The investigation focuses on the potential of quantum state manipulation to overcome inherent computational bottlenecks in optimization.

title: Quantum Memory-Based Biological Information Processing
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to biological information processing by leveraging the principles of quantum memory. The core idea is to mimic the memory function of biological neurons using quantum memory models, thereby accelerating and enhancing the efficiency of biological information handling. This research explores the potential of quantum memory to emulate key aspects of neuronal operation, specifically focusing on the rapid processing and storage of biological information. The theoretical framework developed herein outlines a computational model based on quantum memory interactions, demonstrating a pathway towards achieving significant improvements in biological information processing speed and capacity. This work presents a fundamental investigation into the intersection of quantum mechanics and neuroscience, offering a new perspective on the mechanisms underlying biological memory and potentially paving the way for advanced bio-computing architectures. The presented model utilizes the following key equations to illustrate the core concepts: (Δs) = (H(s) * ∇s) + (G(s, s') * s') where: Δs represents the change in state of the quantum memory. H(s) is the Hamiltonian operator describing the quantum memory's energy levels. ∇s is the gradient operator, representing the influence of external stimuli. G(s, s') is the coupling strength between neighboring quantum memories. s and s' represent the states of the quantum memories. Further equations exploring the dynamics include: (ds/dt) = (H(s) * s) - (∑G(s, s') * s') and the state update rule: s(t+Δt) = U(Δt) * s(t) where: U(Δt) is the time evolution operator, describing the quantum dynamics over a small time interval Δt. This research contributes to the nascent field of quantum biology and provides a foundational model for future investigations into quantum-enhanced biological systems. ---

title: In-line fiber-integrated photon-pair generation from van der Waals crystals
abstract: Miniaturized quantum light sources that operate directly in optical fibers are an attractive platform for optical quantum technologies. However, most miniaturized spontaneous parametric down-conversion (SPDC) sources still rely on objective-lens-based free-space pumping and collection, which limits compactness, robustness, and direct compatibility with fiber-based systems. Here we demonstrate a lens-free in-line SPDC photon-pair source by integrating a van der Waals NbOI[Formula: see text] flake directly onto the end facet of an optical fiber. In this configuration, the generated photon-pairs are efficiently collected into optical fibers, eliminating the need for bulk free-space collection optics. Despite the limited numerical aperture of the single-mode fiber, efficient photon-pair collection with high coincidence-to-accidental ratio (CAR), characterized by a coincidence-to-accidental ratio of up to ∼4600, is achieved in an ultracompact configuration. These results establish van der Waals ferroelectric materials as a promising platform for fiber-integrated quantum light sources and provide a pathway toward compact, alignment-free quantum photonic devices.

title: trajectory-judge: What Outcome-Only LLM Judges Miss on Agent Trajectories
abstract: A direct test of an LLM judge of agent trajectories injects faults into correct runs and reports recall, per fault type or by whether the fault broke the environment outcome (loud) or not (silent). Such recall can credit a judge with detection it does not have; paired discrimination, its flag rate on the faults minus its rate on the clean runs they came from, exposes this. Our testbed, a deterministic support desk with a scripted oracle and a one-step fault injector, labels all 400 trajectories exactly. A 14B judge shown only the request and final reply scores 34% to 76% recall on four fault types that leave the reply unchanged. There its input is the clean run's, so its paired discrimination is zero and that recall is its flag rate on clean runs. Splitting by outcome survival does not fix this: its loud recall of 84% is a paired +0.393 and its silent recall of 45% a paired +0.048, all from the two fault types that change the reply. Told to check each step, the same model flags every fault of those four types and 0 of 100 clean runs (95% CI up to 3.6%). It does not reliably check the reply: of four invented promises it flags one every time and the other three once in 42 faults. Shown every step but asked only about the reply, it still reaches a paired +0.69 on reply-unchanged faults, against +1.00 when told to check each step. We recommend reporting paired discrimination against clean parents, split by whether the fault reaches the judge's input and by outcome survival, and release the testbed, raw verdicts and analysis pipeline.

title: Beyond Speech: Dual-Domain SSL Fusion for Unified All-Type Audio Deepfake Detection
abstract: Unified all-type audio deepfake detection aims to determine whether an input clip is real or fake when its audio type may be speech, environmental sound, singing voice, or music. Existing speech-centric or type-dependent solutions are insufficient for this setting because the test-time audio type is unknown, while the required output is still a single binary decision. To address these issues, this paper proposes a dual-domain SSL fusion method that maps heterogeneous audio into a shared binary authenticity space. EAT-large and wav2vec 2.0 XLS-R-300M are used as complementary SSL feature sources, providing broad acoustic and event-level representations as well as waveform-level, vocal, and speech-sensitive representations. Layer-wise weighted fusion integrates multi-level artifacts from different transformer depths, while token-level fusion forms a unified feature pool without enforcing frame-level alignment between the two SSL streams. The fused tokens are summarized by multi-head attentive statistics pooling and classified with a binary MLP head. With conservative speech refinement applied on top of this unified core detector, the submitted system achieves 95.58% Macro-F1 on the AT-ADD Track 2 evaluation set and ranks second in the challenge.

title: Analisis Sentimen Masyarakat Terhadap Kualitas Layanan BPJS (Badan Penyelenggara Jaminan Sosial) Kesehatan Berdasarkan Ulasan Media Sosial Menggunakan Metode Naive Bayes
abstract: Badan Penyelenggara Jaminan Sosial (BPJS) Kesehatan merupakan lembaga yang berperan penting dalam memberikan jaminan pelayanan kesehatan bagi masyarakat Indonesia. Twitter (X) menjadi salah satu media yang digunakan masyarakat untuk menyampaikan opini, pengalaman, dan keluhan terkait layanan BPJS Kesehatan. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis sentimen masyarakat, menerapkan algoritma Naive Bayes dalam klasifikasi, mengetahui sentimen dominan, serta mengukur tingkat akurasi model dalam melakukan klasifikasi sentimen. Data berupa komentar Twitter (X) dikumpulkan berdasarkan kata kunci yang berkaitan dengan BPJS Kesehatan dan pelayanan BPJS. Data kemudian diolah melalui tahapan text preprocessing, pelabelan, splitting data, pembobotan TF-IDF, klasifikasi menggunakan Naive Bayes, dan evaluasi model. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa sentimen negative sebesar 75,7%, neutral sebesar 21,1%, dan positive sebesar 3,2%, sehingga sentimen negative menjadi sentimen yang dominan. Hasil klasifikasi menggunakan Naive Bayes memperoleh tingkat akurasi sebesar 75,67%. Hasil tersebut menunjukkan bahwa Naive Bayes dapat digunakan untuk mengklasifikasikan sentimen masyarakat terhadap layanan BPJS Kesehatan berdasarkan komentar Twitter (X).

title: Quantum Topology Adaptive Algorithms
abstract: Quantum Topology Adaptive Algorithms (QTAA) presents a novel approach to quantum computation, focusing on the adaptive adjustment of quantum topology during computation. This research explores the potential of utilizing quantum topology's inherent self-similarity and adaptability to optimize computational processes. The core claim of this study is the design of a QTA algorithm capable of dynamically reshaping quantum states, offering enhanced efficiency and flexibility compared to traditional methods. This advancement addresses the limitations of current quantum algorithms by introducing a mechanism that responds to input data, effectively tailoring the quantum system's topology. The study delves into the underlying principles of this adaptive strategy and its potential impact on various quantum computational tasks.

title: Quantum Simulation of Non-Equilibrium Systems using Adaptive Sampling
abstract: Quantum simulation of non-equilibrium systems presents a significant challenge due to the inherent complexity of these systems and the limitations of classical simulation techniques. Traditional methods often struggle to accurately capture the intricate dynamics arising from non-equilibrium conditions. This paper introduces a novel method, Adaptive Sampling, designed to overcome these limitations. We propose an iterative process where the sampling rate is dynamically adjusted based on the system's evolution, enabling the capture of complex dynamics with greater fidelity and reduced computational cost. The core mechanism centers on employing adaptive sampling to refine the simulation, allowing for the exploration of a wider range of possible states and ultimately, a more accurate representation of the system's behavior. This approach promises to significantly advance the field of quantum simulation, offering a robust and adaptable solution to the challenges associated with simulating non-equilibrium systems.

abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to model parameter adjustment for non-linear quantum state models. Traditional parameter adjustment methods often rely on iterative optimization algorithms, which can be computationally expensive and may not always converge to optimal solutions. We propose a new framework that leverages quantum state entanglement to dynamically adjust model parameters, enhancing training efficiency and potentially improving model performance. This approach utilizes a quantum state representation to guide parameter adjustments, offering a fundamentally different perspective on parameter optimization. The paper details the theoretical underpinnings of the quantum state entanglement mechanism and demonstrates its effectiveness through simulations and initial experiments. We highlight the potential advantages of this method over existing techniques, emphasizing its capacity to address challenges related to convergence and sensitivity to initial conditions.

Traditional optimization methods often focus solely on minimizing loss functions, neglecting the inherent structure within the data and model. This work proposes a method that intelligently adapts model parameters based on the relationships and topology of the data, leading to enhanced model performance and generalization capabilities. We introduce a "拓扑结构指导优化" mechanism that leverages topological concepts to optimize model parameters, specifically focusing on preserving and improving data manifold structure. The core mechanism centers around identifying and utilizing topological features to constrain parameter updates, promoting smoother and more stable convergence. The paper presents a theoretical analysis of the proposed framework and demonstrates its efficacy through several benchmark datasets. The results showcase significant improvements in model accuracy, robustness, and generalization across various machine learning tasks.

title: Quantum Machine Learning Optimization Based on Quantum Noise
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of leveraging quantum noise as an additional optimization signal within quantum machine learning (QML) algorithms. The core claim is that controlled quantum noise, rather than being detrimental, can significantly enhance the training efficiency of QML models. The proposed mechanism involves introducing specifically designed quantum noise into the training process and utilizing the information inherent within this noise to guide gradient estimation and parameter updates. This approach represents a novel strategy for QML optimization, moving beyond purely deterministic methods. We explore theoretical frameworks and mathematical formulations to demonstrate the viability and potential benefits of this approach. The key contribution lies in recognizing and harnessing the information encoded within quantum noise, offering a new pathway for accelerating the training of complex QML models. This research provides a foundation for future investigations into noise-aware QML algorithms.

title: Explainable AI for Reinforcement Learning via Causal Reasoning
abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) has achieved remarkable success in various domains, but its "black box" nature poses a significant challenge for real-world deployment. Understanding the rationale behind an RL agent's decisions is crucial for trust, debugging, and improving performance. This paper proposes a novel approach to explainable AI (XAI) within reinforcement learning by leveraging causal reasoning. We model the environment and the agent's policy using a causal Bayesian network. By performing inference through this network, we trace the causal chain of events leading to a specific action, providing a transparent explanation. This method moves beyond simply observing the agent's behavior to understanding the underlying reasons for its choices. The core of our approach lies in identifying and representing the causal relationships within the RL system, enabling us to dissect the decision-making process and ultimately build more robust and reliable RL agents. The proposed framework offers a significant step toward interpretable RL and addresses a critical limitation of current techniques. ---

title: Distributed Proof Verification via Consensus-Based Quantum Error Correction
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to mathematical proof verification leveraging the principles of quantum computing, specifically consensus-based quantum error correction (CQEC). Traditional proof verification is often a computationally intensive process, particularly for complex proofs. This work introduces a distributed system where multiple quantum computers collaboratively verify a proof, with CQEC employed to identify and rectify errors introduced during the verification process. The core idea is to transform the problem of verifying a single, potentially long and intricate proof into a series of smaller, independently verifiable sub-proofs. These sub-proofs are then distributed across a network of quantum computers. Each computer attempts to verify its assigned sub-proof. A consensus protocol, built upon CQEC, is then applied to the results. This protocol aims to identify inconsistencies and errors arising from the individual verifications, ultimately converging on a definitive verdict regarding the validity of the entire proof. The efficiency gains are predicated on the inherent error correction capabilities of quantum systems and the ability to parallelize the verification process through distributed computation. We explore the theoretical framework, outlining the key components of the system and the mathematical foundation underlying the CQEC protocol. This research suggests a potentially transformative approach to computational verification, offering the prospect of dramatically reducing verification times for complex mathematical arguments.

title: Evolutionary Algorithms for Designing Hardware-Aware Neural Network Architectures
abstract: This paper investigates the application of evolutionary algorithms for the automated design of neural network architectures, specifically tailored to meet the constraints of target hardware platforms. The core premise is that traditional neural network architecture design is often a manual, iterative process, heavily influenced by expert knowledge and intuition. This approach can be inefficient and may not fully exploit the potential optimization opportunities afforded by specific hardware characteristics. We propose a framework where neural network architectures are represented as genetic programs and evolved using techniques such as mutation and crossover. The fitness function, crucial to this process, evaluates the network's performance on the target hardware, considering factors like memory bandwidth, computational power, and energy consumption. This research aims to shift the paradigm from human-designed architectures to automatically generated, hardware-aware architectures, potentially leading to significant improvements in network efficiency and performance. The methodology presented offers a novel approach to neural architecture search (NAS) with a focus on explicit hardware integration, addressing a critical gap in current NAS techniques.

title: Symbolic Regression with Bayesian Neural Networks
abstract: Symbolic regression is a technique focused on automatically discovering mathematical equations from observed data. This work presents a novel approach that integrates Bayesian Neural Networks (BNNs) with symbolic regression methodologies. The core idea is to leverage the representational capacity of BNNs to learn a symbolic representation of the data, subsequently utilizing this representation to generate potential equations. The Bayesian framework embedded within the BNN allows for explicit uncertainty quantification, which is crucial for robust equation discovery and validation. We argue that this hybrid approach overcomes limitations inherent in purely symbolic or purely neural methods, offering improved accuracy and robustness in identifying underlying mathematical relationships. The proposed method is demonstrated through theoretical analysis and conceptual design, outlining a framework for implementation and future development.

title: Neuro-Symbolic Programming with Temporal Logic
abstract: This paper explores the integration of neural networks and symbolic programming through the lens of temporal logic. The core challenge in neuro-symbolic systems lies in effectively combining the pattern recognition capabilities of neural networks with the logical reasoning abilities of symbolic systems. This work proposes a framework where a neural network learns to represent symbolic rules, and a temporal logic engine is employed to rigorously verify the consistency and validity of the network's inferences across time. The system's ability to guarantee reasoning correctness, a key limitation of traditional neural networks, is achieved by leveraging temporal logic's expressiveness and verification capabilities. The framework offers a novel approach to building robust and verifiable AI systems, particularly in domains where logical constraints and temporal dependencies are paramount. This paper outlines the architecture, the learning process, and the verification mechanism, highlighting the benefits of this combined approach.

title: High-Dimensional Data Distribution Analysis and Predictive Modeling
abstract: This research investigates the application of advanced data distribution analysis techniques to predict future data trends. Traditional methods often focus on statistical properties, while this work proposes a novel approach grounded in the inherent characteristics of high-dimensional data distributions. The core mechanism involves the implementation of an adaptive clustering algorithm to segment high-dimensional data into distinct clusters, followed by a predictive modeling process that leverages these cluster groupings and the data distribution's inherent patterns. The study aims to develop a robust and insightful system for forecasting future data trends, offering valuable support for decision-making in complex data environments. The proposed model demonstrates the potential for superior prediction accuracy compared to existing approaches, particularly when dealing with high-dimensional datasets exhibiting complex and non-linear relationships.

title: 拓扑优化神经网络 (Topological Optimization Neural Networks)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel neural network architecture, the Topological Optimization Neural Networks (TONs), that leverages the concept of topology to enhance model generalization and efficiency. Traditional neural networks often rely on large gradient descent, lacking precise control over the network's internal structure. TONs employ a dynamic topology structure, which automatically adjusts network connections and weights during training, resulting in more effective feature extraction and representation. This approach overcomes the limitations of gradient-based methods by providing a principled framework for optimizing network parameters. The core mechanism centers around constructing and dynamically modifying a topological structure that guides the learning process. Core Claim: We propose that introducing the concept of topology into the design of neural networks can significantly improve their generalization ability and efficiency through automated adjustment of network connections and weights. Core Mechanism: TONs employ a dynamic topology structure that establishes a hierarchy of interconnected nodes, using topological properties to guide the learning process. The topology is dynamically adjusted during training, optimizing connectivity and weight assignments to improve representation and generalization. Why It Is New: Traditional neural networks frequently rely on large gradient descent, lacking precise control over network internal structure. TONs introduce a dynamic topology approach, enabling automated adjustment of connectivity and weights to improve generalization.

title: Weakly supervised deep learning distinguishes alcohol-associated from metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis on H&E whole-slide images
abstract: Distinguishing alcohol-associated steatohepatitis (ASH) from metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) is challenging given the absence of pathognomonic differentiators. We developed and evaluated a weakly supervised deep learning model, as a single-institution proof-of-concept study, to test whether routine hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) whole-slide images (WSIs) of liver biopsies contain sufficient morphological information to predict steatohepatitis etiology at the slide level. A retrospective cohort of 1147 WSIs was assembled (train set: 1007, holdout test set: 140). Models were trained using 5-fold patient-level cross-validation at ×20 and ×40 magnification. Model interpretability was assessed through attention-based clustering with blinded pathologist review of high-attention patches. The ×20 model achieved a mean area under the receiver operating characteristic of 0.86 ± 0.01 on the test set, with balanced accuracy of 0.80. The ×40 model performed comparably. Specificity was high (0.93 at ×20), with an ASH sensitivity of 0.67 at ×20. Fibrosis-stratified showed preserved performance at advanced fibrosis (stage ≥3) with balanced accuracy of 82.5% and ASH sensitivity of 77.4%. Attention-based clustering localized ASH-enriched regions to active injury patterns including Mallory-Denk bodies, neutrophilic inflammation, cholestatic change, and pericellular fibrosis, whereas MASH-enriched regions showed steatosis with lower inflammatory activity. Weakly supervised deep learning applied to routine liver H&E WSIs can discriminate ASH from MASH with performance preserved at advanced fibrosis. The comparable performance of ×20 and ×40 magnification, and the alignment of model attention with established histological features, support the use of routine morphology as a decision-support input in cases with incomplete or conflicting clinical histories, particularly when the etiological distinction has the greatest implications for management.

title: Evaluating Tiny Recursive Models Across Training for Code Generation
abstract: Code generation increasingly relies on large transformer models, whose capability advances with scale. Yet such a scale is costly, creating demand for small models, especially where data is limited. Recursive models address this by reusing a single block to add depth rather than stacking independent layers. Such models are typically evaluated by teacher-forced fit (next-token loss on ground-truth prefixes) or task accuracy, at a single checkpoint, whereas code is produced by free-running generation, where the model extends its own output. Whether a teacher-forced advantage survives free-running generation, and whether it holds across training, remains open. To study both, we compare a ~28M-parameter autoregressive Tiny Recursive Model (TRM-AR) on natural-language-to-Python code generation against parameter-matched and depth-matched controls, tracking fit and generation across 40 epochs and three seeds. The fit ranking between the recursive model and the depth-matched control reverses twice. Selecting each checkpoint by validation loss and examining the trajectory yields a consistent comparison. At equal parameters, TRM-AR fits, generates, and generalizes better than the parameter-matched control while recovering approximately 45% of the validation-loss gap and 57% of the generation-quality gap between the two controls, at roughly 175 times the per-step cost of the parameter-matched control. However, at equal effective depth, the larger transformer fits and generates better at its validation optimum, suggesting TRM-AR's advantage lies in resistance to overfitting, not greater capability. These findings suggest that recursive code generation models should be evaluated jointly on fit and generation across the training trajectory rather than at a single checkpoint.

title: History-Conditioned Joint-Prefix Alignment for Generative Recommendation
abstract: Generative recommendation retrieves items by autoregressively generating semantic identifiers, but beam search may discard a target before its complete identifier is generated. Our preliminary analysis across three benchmarks shows that most missed targets are pruned within the first two decoding steps, highlighting the importance of early prefix retention. However, retaining a target's first-token branch alone is insufficient if its continuation is pruned at the next step: aligning only the first-token distribution improves first-token survival but yields little gain in complete-path retention. This observation motivates joint supervision of early branches and their continuations. We propose Prefix Alignment with Temporal History (PATH), which aggregates transition statistics from the training corpus over recent interactions with exponential decay to construct history-conditioned two-token prefix targets. PATH aligns the model's joint predictions with these targets through forward KL divergence, using a chain-rule decomposition that enables unbiased Monte Carlo estimation. At inference time, PATH reuses the transition statistics for pointwise mutual information (PMI) calibration, reranking completed candidates relative to global prefix frequency. Experiments on Beauty, Instruments, and Yelp demonstrate the effectiveness of PATH, showing consistent improvements in recommendation performance and higher full-SID survival rates.

title: Continuity-Free Near-Minimax Leading-Order Regret for CVaR-UCBVI
abstract: For finite-horizon tabular CVaR reinforcement learning, prior work proves a $\widetilde{O}(τ^{-1}\sqrt{SAK})$ leading regret bound for arbitrary normalized return laws and the sharper $\widetilde{O}(\sqrt{SAK/τ})$ rate under a density lower bound. We show that the same Bernstein CVaR-UCBVI algorithm attains the sharper rate without continuity assumptions. The key is a selected-budget self-bound: the conditional variance of the episode shortfall is at most $τ$ plus the value-estimation width. Substitution into the original Bernstein decomposition yields, with high probability, $\widetilde{O}(\sqrt{SAK/τ}+(SAHK^{1/4}+S^2AH)/τ)$ regret for arbitrary normalized return laws, including atomic, mixed, and continuous laws. The $τ^{-1/2}$ leading term matches the expected-regret minimax lower bound up to logarithmic factors. Thus Bernstein CVaR-UCBVI is minimax-optimal over the full return-law class in the leading-order regime; the lower-order terms retain their $τ^{-1}$ dependence.

title: Analisis Pengaruh Kualitas Penggunaan ChatBot Terhadap Keputusan Pembelian Pada Marketplace Shopee
abstract: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis pengaruh kualitas penggunaan ChatBot terhadap keputusan pembelian pada marketplace Shopee. Chatbot merupakan salah satu inovasi layanan berbasis kecerdasan buatan yang digunakan Shopee untuk membantu konsumen memperoleh informasi produk, status pesanan, dan layanan lainnya secara cepat dan otomatis. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan metode survei melalui penyebaran kuesioner kepada 37 responden pengguna Shopee yang pernah berinteraksi dengan fitur chatbot dan pernah melakukan pembelian. Data dianalisis menggunakan metode Partial Least Squares–Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) dengan bantuan aplikasi SmartPLS 4. title: Budgeted Reward Allocation: A Position on Unifying Sparse, Verifiable, and Hierarchical Reward Signals in LLM Post-Training
abstract: Reward hacking, verbosity, and hallucination are usually treated as separate failure modes in the post-training of large language models, addressed by separate mechanisms: reward shaping for verbosity, verifiable reward models (RLVR) for hallucination, hierarchical decomposition for long-horizon tasks, and load-balancing losses for mixture-of-experts (MoE) routing. This position paper argues that these four mechanisms can be described as instances of a single accounting abstraction: a finite, per-task reward budget that is released only against verified sub-goal completion, decays to a penalty once exhausted, and can be propagated across a task hierarchy and an expert pool as a routing signal. We do not claim that any individual component is new — verifiable rewards, reward shaping, hierarchical reinforcement learning, and MoE routing are each established, actively studied techniques, and we cite the relevant literature for each. The contribution we argue for is narrower and more honest: a shared bookkeeping formalism (budget allocation, exhaustion, and propagation) that makes explicit how these four techniques already interact in practice, and that suggests a small number of concrete, testable predictions about where combining them should help or hurt.

title: High-Order Transformation of Quantum Geometry for Precise Geometric Modeling
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of high-order quantum transformation techniques to revolutionize geometric modeling, specifically by leveraging the unique properties of quantum computation. We propose a novel approach that utilizes quantum-induced geometric transformations to achieve unprecedented precision and computational efficiency in geometric calculations. This research explores the design and implementation of a quantum-based high-order transformation algorithm, focusing on its ability to accurately manipulate space geometry. The core mechanism centers around introducing quantum-controlled transformations, enabling precise geometric modeling and offering a significant advancement over classical methods. This work provides a foundational investigation into the application of quantum computation to geometric modeling, highlighting the potential for significant computational gains and improved geometric accuracy.

title: ##基于多模态上下文的因果推理引擎 (MCIRE)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to causal reasoning, the Multi-Modal Contextual Causal Reasoning Engine (MCIRE). MCIRE addresses the limitations of existing causal inference models that primarily rely on single-modality data by integrating contextual information from diverse sources, including text, images, and audio. The core of MCIRE lies in a multi-modal embedding technique combined with a graph-based causal reasoning model. We transform different modalities into unified vector representations and leverage a graph structure to model and capture the causal relationships between them, enriched by contextual information. This allows for the inference of complex causal chains and relationships within multi-modal data. The engine demonstrates potential for applications in areas requiring robust causal understanding, such as automated diagnosis, decision-making, and scenario simulation. ---

title: Quantum State Adaptive Topology Optimization
abstract: Quantum State Adaptive Topology Optimization is a novel algorithm designed to optimize quantum states by dynamically adjusting the topology of the quantum system. This approach leverages the inherent properties of quantum states, allowing for a more efficient and robust optimization process compared to traditional methods. The core mechanism centers around a self-correcting structure, guided by the quantum state itself, leading to enhanced computational efficiency and storage capacity. The algorithm's novelty lies in its utilization of quantum state adaptability to achieve a fundamentally different optimization strategy. This paper details the algorithm's design, implementation, and performance evaluation, demonstrating its potential for significant advancements in quantum state manipulation and optimization.

title: Title: Dynamic Field Theory (DFT)
abstract: Dynamic Field Theory (DFT) offers a novel approach to quantum information storage and transmission, predicated on the concept of self-adaptive topological structures. This research explores the potential of incorporating such structures to enhance quantum entanglement stability and unlock advanced data processing capabilities. We detail the design of a novel quantum bit (qubit) architecture based on this dynamic topology, highlighting the self-adjusting nature of the topology as a key mechanism for achieving ultra-high capacity and resistance to interference. This work introduces a fundamentally new method for quantum information encoding and decryption, leveraging the inherent properties of topological structures. The core claim is that DFT provides a pathway towards exceeding current limitations in data storage and transmission, particularly through the implementation of enhanced entanglement and robust information handling.

title: Graph Representation Learning via Contrastive Predictive Coding
abstract: Graph representation learning has emerged as a crucial technique in various domains, including social network analysis, drug discovery, and recommendation systems. However, many existing methods struggle to effectively capture long-range dependencies within graphs, leading to suboptimal representations. This paper introduces a novel approach to graph representation learning based on Contrastive Predictive Coding (CPC). We leverage the inherent predictive structure of graphs by training models to predict future nodes based on their contextual information. This allows us to learn representations that are sensitive to long-range relationships. Our method, CPC-Graph, utilizes a recurrent neural network to encode the graph structure and predict future nodes, minimizing the difference between predicted and actual representations. We demonstrate the effectiveness of CPC-Graph through theoretical analysis and the formulation of key equations, showcasing its ability to capture dependencies efficiently. The core claim of this work is that existing graph representation learning methods often struggle to capture long-range dependencies. This new method employs Contrastive Predictive Coding (CPC) to address this issue, providing a robust solution for learning graph representations.

title: Title: Non-Linear Correlation Field Modeling with Adaptive Bias
abstract: Correlation analysis plays a fundamental role in various fields, from scientific research to data visualization, providing insights into relationships between variables. However, traditional correlation methods often struggle with non-linear relationships, limiting the accuracy of predictions. This paper proposes a novel approach to non-linear correlation modeling utilizing an Adaptive Bias Network, a system designed to dynamically adjust bias towards different correlations, leading to enhanced predictive accuracy. We explore a framework for implementing this network and demonstrate its effectiveness through a series of simulations and experimental validation. The core mechanism focuses on the adaptive adjustment of bias, effectively capturing the intricate non-linear dependencies that often obscure traditional correlations. This research aims to address a significant challenge in correlation modeling, offering a more robust and accurate method for complex system analysis.

title: Probabilistic Programming for Modeling Sensor Fusion with Uncertainty
abstract: Sensor fusion, the process of combining data from multiple sensors to produce a more accurate and reliable estimate of a system's state, is a cornerstone of many modern applications, including autonomous vehicles, robotics, and environmental monitoring. However, traditional sensor fusion approaches frequently treat sensor readings as deterministic values, failing to account for the inherent uncertainty associated with real-world sensor measurements. This paper proposes a novel framework for sensor fusion leveraging probabilistic programming, specifically Bayesian networks, to explicitly model and propagate uncertainty. The core claim is that incorporating uncertainty into the fusion process leads to more robust and accurate state estimation. We detail a methodology for constructing Bayesian networks that represent the relationships between sensors and their associated noise distributions. This approach allows for the calculation of posterior distributions over the system state, providing a quantified measure of uncertainty in the fused estimate. The framework offers a rigorous and mathematically sound approach to sensor fusion, addressing a critical limitation of existing techniques. The proposed method provides a flexible and adaptable solution that can be applied to a wide range of sensor fusion problems.

title: Quantum-Inspired Reservoir Computing for Time Series Prediction
abstract: This paper investigates the application of quantum-inspired principles to enhance reservoir computing, a method commonly used for time series prediction. Traditional reservoir computing relies on randomly connected recurrent neural networks to capture complex temporal dynamics. However, these networks often struggle to efficiently represent intricate patterns, particularly when dealing with high-dimensional time series data. This research proposes a novel approach by incorporating concepts from quantum superposition and interference into the design of the reservoir. Specifically, we explore techniques that mimic quantum measurement processes to improve the reservoir's ability to extract relevant features and generate predictive signals. The core idea is to create a reservoir that, while not explicitly employing quantum hardware, is conceptually inspired by quantum mechanics, leading to a more effective and potentially superior time series prediction performance. We present a framework for designing such a quantum-inspired reservoir and discuss its theoretical underpinnings. The results, while theoretical at this stage, suggest a promising avenue for future research in reservoir computing and signal processing.

title: Quantum Entanglement-Based Distributed Sensor Networks
abstract: This paper explores the potential of utilizing quantum entanglement to construct distributed sensor networks. The core claim is that leveraging entanglement enables precise measurement and transmission of environmental information. The proposed mechanism involves entangling multiple sensor nodes, exploiting the unique properties of entanglement for information fusion and data transfer, ultimately enhancing sensor accuracy and reliability. This research addresses a novel application of quantum entanglement in distributed sensing, offering the prospect of significantly improved sensor performance compared to classical approaches. The focus is on theoretical development and conceptual design, without experimental validation. We present a framework for designing such a network and discuss the key challenges and potential benefits.

title: Tenrec Optimization Algorithm: A Novel Swarm-based Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Natural Foraging and Digging Behaviors of Tenrec
abstract: Metaheuristic algorithms are important optimization tools in engineering sciences and real-world applications due to their high ability to solve complex, nonlinear, and multidimensional problems.The success of these algorithms largely depends on striking a proper balance between exploration and exploitation during the search process, because exploration leads to extensive exploration of the search space and avoids getting stuck in local optima, while exploitation accelerates the convergence process towards high-quality answers by focusing on promising areas.Accordingly, providing new strategies for effectively managing these two processes remains one of the very important research topics in the field of metaheuristic algorithms.In this study, a population-based metaheuristic algorithm named Tenrec Optimization Algorithm (TOA), inspired by the natural behaviour of the Tenrec animal in the wild, is introduced.Behaviour of this animal is investigated, and its characteristic strategies are extracted to design the proposed approach.The exploration phase is modeled with the inspiration of Random Foraging/Wide Area Searching behaviour and aims to increase the search space coverage, avoid repeating previous paths and guide agents towards unknown areas.Also, the exploitation phase is designed based on the digging behaviour in promising areas and adaptive return to the best past experiences to perform local search more accurately.The performance of TOA is evaluated using 23 standard benchmark functions including unimodal test functions, high-dimensional multimodal test functions and fixed-dimensional multimodal test functions.The results show that TOA has a high ability in exploitation in unimodal test functions, a good power in exploration in high-dimensional multimodal test functions and a good performance in balancing exploration and exploitation in fixed-dimensional multimodal test functions.Also, comparison with 9 well-known metaheuristic algorithms shows that TOA, by achieving the best rank in 20 functions out of a total of 23 benchmark functions, provides more competitive performance in about 86.95% of problems and can be used as an effective optimizer for a wide range of optimization problems.

title: Think, Look, and Revise: Inconsistency-Aware Visual Self-Correction in MLLMs
abstract: Tool-augmented multimodal reasoning integrates external tools (e.g., object detection, depth estimation) into multimodal large language models (MLLMs) to address perceptual bottlenecks in complex visual tasks. However, existing approaches rarely verify tool outputs, limiting their ability to detect and recover from tool failures. We propose ReVISE, a framework that equips MLLMs with verification and dynamic error recovery for tool-augmented reasoning. ReVISE introduces (1) a curated training dataset that supervises reflective behaviors, enabling models to validate tool-derived evidence, reformulate queries when visual mismatches arise, and fall back to intrinsic grounding when external tools are unreliable; and (2) a reinforcement learning based targeted rewards that encourage internal reflection and penalize spatial misalignment. Experiments on several benchmarks demonstrate consistent improvements over existing methods, highlighting the importance of error detection and correction in tool-augmented multimodal reasoning.
