title: Dynamic-Robust Photometric-Semantic Reconstruction for Open-Vocabulary 3D Scene Understanding
abstract: The integration of novel view synthesis (NVS) and open-vocabulary segmentation (OVS) has recently yielded powerful feed-forward 3D foundation models. However, their inherent reliance on static-scene assumptions leads to severe misalignment of spatial features in unconstrained dynamic environments. To bridge this critical gap, we propose SPAR, a novel joint semantic-geometric encoding architecture that explicitly isolates transient dynamic noise prior to latent space aggregation. Furthermore, we introduce a dynamic-region-aware end-to-end training paradigm that structurally couples motion estimation with multi-view visual and semantic learning. This unified approach enables the network to inherently resolve motion conflicts and distill multi-view consistent, temporally stable scene representations from dynamic inputs. Extensive experiments on the challenging D-RE10K benchmark demonstrate that SPAR achieves state-of-the-art performance. Our end-to-end approach achieves exceptional novel view synthesis quality, yielding a PSNR of 22.15 dB and 23.33 dB given only 3 and 4 input views respectively. Despite being trained in a self-supervised manner, our model achieves an mIoU of 88.5% for motion mask prediction. Furthermore, our analysis reveals a strong inter-task synergy between photometric scene reconstruction and semantic understanding, where semantic synthesis learning consistently enhances photometric fidelity in novel view rendering. Code will be available at https://github.com/dmucby/SPAR.

title: Composition Over Inheritance: A Narrative Review of the Entity-Component-System Pattern in Game Engine Architecture
abstract: The Entity-Component-System pattern is game engineering's answer to the deepest architectural question of interactive software: how to organize thousands of heterogeneous, constantly mutating objects without drowning in inheritance hierarchies---entities as identifiers, components as pure data, and systems as the logic that transforms the data. This article presents a narrative review of the primary literature of that pattern, from the interface-design and pattern corpora that shaped its thinking---Krasner and Pope's model-view-controller, the Gang of Four's design patterns with their composition-over-inheritance doctrine, and Buschmann and colleagues' pattern-oriented software architecture---through the game industry's founding documents: Bilas' data-oriented, data-driven component system presented at the 2002 Game Developers Conference and Adams' evolve your hierarchy, the two texts that crystallized the shift from deep class trees to composition, West's refactoring game entities with components, which carried the pattern to the magazine mainstream, and the engine corpora: Gregory's game engine architecture, Nystrom's game programming patterns, Acton's data-oriented design and C++, Fabian's data-oriented design, Martin's clean architecture, and Unity's Entity Component System documentation, which industrialized the pattern for mass development. The synthesis is organized around three themes: the inheritance crisis, in which the deep hierarchies of object-oriented engines failed at scale; the composition solution, in which entities, components, and systems separated identity, state, and behavior; and the data-oriented execution, in which cache-aware memory layout turned the pattern into a performance architecture. It is concluded that ECS is software architecture's natural experiment---a pattern invented, refined, and validated inside the game industry's pressure cooker---and that its separation of data from logic has become the modern engine's organizing principle.

evidence.title: Composition Over Inheritance: A Narrative Review of the Entity-Component-System Pattern in Game Engine Architecture
evidence.abstract: The Entity-Component-System pattern is game engineering's answer to the deepest architectural question of interactive software: how to organize thousands of heterogeneous, constantly mutating objects without drowning in inheritance hierarchies---entities as identifiers, components as pure data, and systems as the logic that transforms the data. This article presents a narrative review of the primary literature of that pattern, from the interface-design and pattern corpora that shaped its thinking---Krasner and Pope's model-view-controller, the Gang of Four's design patterns with their composition-over-inheritance doctrine, and Buschmann and colleagues' pattern-oriented software architecture---through the game industry's founding documents: Bilas' data-oriented, data-driven component system presented at the 2002 Game Developers Conference and Adams' evolve your hierarchy, the two texts that crystallized the shift from deep class trees to composition, West's refactoring game entities with components, which carried the pattern to the magazine mainstream, and the engine corpora: Gregory's game engine architecture, Nystrom's game programming patterns, Acton's data-oriented design and C++, Fabian's data-oriented design, Martin's clean architecture, and Unity's Entity Component System documentation, which industrialized the pattern for mass development. The synthesis is organized around three themes: the inheritance crisis, in which the deep hierarchies of object-oriented engines failed at scale; the composition solution, in which entities, components, and systems separated identity, state, and behavior; and the data-oriented execution, in which cache-aware memory layout turned the pattern into a performance architecture. It is concluded that ECS is software architecture's natural experiment---a pattern invented, refined, and validated inside the game industry's pressure cooker---and that its separation of data from logic has become the modern engine's organizing principle.

title: High-Dimensional Topology and Quantum Algorithm Connection
abstract: This paper investigates the synergistic relationship between high-dimensional topology and quantum algorithms. We explore how the inherent properties of high-dimensional topological spaces can be leveraged to enhance the efficiency and stability of quantum algorithms. The core focus is to develop novel optimization strategies predicated on topological constraints, resulting in improved performance compared to traditional approaches. The research utilizes a framework where high-dimensional topology serves as a guiding principle for algorithm design, ultimately aiming to create more robust and computationally effective quantum systems. The investigation will delve into the mathematical underpinnings of this connection, providing a theoretical foundation for practical application. This work contributes to the advancement of quantum algorithm design by offering a new perspective on how topology can impact quantum performance.

title: 基于自适应神经网络的复杂系统响应建模
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to complex system response modeling leveraging adaptive neural networks. Traditional methods often rely on static parameters, limiting their ability to capture the dynamic behavior of complex systems. We propose a dynamic adjustment mechanism for neural network weights and connections, enabling a more accurate and flexible representation of system responses. The core mechanism focuses on real-time adaptation to the system's dynamics, resulting in improved predictive performance compared to static models. This work demonstrates the efficacy of this approach through a series of simulations and initial experimental results focused on a simplified dynamic system. The paper concludes with a discussion of the potential applications and future research directions.

title: Simulating Evolution Algorithm and Deep Reinforcement Learning Hybrid Framework
abstract: This paper proposes a novel hybrid framework integrating the Simulated Evolution Algorithm (SEA) and Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) to tackle complex optimization problems. The core idea is to leverage SEA's global search capability for initial exploration and DRL's local optimization prowess for refining solutions. The framework operates through an iterative process: SEA generates a diverse population of potential solutions, and DRL is then employed to optimize individual solutions or subsets of the population. Crucially, the parameters of both algorithms are iteratively updated based on their performance, enabling a synergistic evolution. We demonstrate the framework's effectiveness through theoretical analysis and a detailed explanation of the mechanisms involved. The key contribution lies in establishing a robust and adaptable method for combining these two powerful techniques, promising improved efficiency and solution quality compared to using them independently. This work provides a foundational approach for future research exploring the synergy between evolutionary and reinforcement learning methods.

title: Hyper-Real Matrix: A Novel Matrix Computation Framework for Advanced Geometric Transformations
abstract: This paper introduces the Hyper-Real Matrix (HRM) – a novel matrix computation framework designed to handle complex geometric transformations beyond the capabilities of traditional matrix operations. Leveraging the unique properties of quantum computing, the HRM aims to accelerate computation and expand the range of geometric transformations through optimized calculations. The core mechanism centers around the introduction of a "Hyper-Real Matrix," which fundamentally alters the mathematical representation of matrices and enables a new approach to geometric manipulation. This research explores the potential of the HRM to revolutionize various fields, particularly those involving intricate geometric modeling and simulations. The paper details the theoretical foundation, implementation details, and preliminary experimental results demonstrating the framework's capabilities.

title: 基于自适应的量子计算的误差分析
abstract: Quantum computing holds immense promise for revolutionizing various fields, but its practical realization faces significant challenges related to error rates. Traditional error analysis methods often rely on static models, failing to fully exploit the inherent adaptability of quantum systems. This paper proposes a novel approach to error analysis based on the adaptive properties of quantum states, aiming to significantly enhance the reliability and efficiency of quantum computation. We detail a dynamic error analysis framework utilizing quantum state self-adaptation to provide robust error prediction and control strategies. The core mechanism involves mapping quantum states to error patterns and dynamically adjusting control parameters to mitigate these patterns. The study demonstrates the effectiveness of this approach through simulations and a simplified experimental setup, showcasing potential improvements in error detection and correction. The findings highlight the advantages of this dynamic, adaptive method for tackling the complexities inherent in quantum systems.

title: Quantum Machine Learning: Error Analysis and Correction of Decoherence Errors
abstract: Decoherence poses a significant challenge to the practical application of quantum machine learning (QML) algorithms. This paper delves into the analysis and correction of decoherence errors, a core mechanism in QML. We establish a comprehensive error model based on the quantum mechanical phenomenon of decoherence, quantifying its impact on algorithm performance. The model incorporates the time evolution of quantum states under the influence of environmental noise, represented by the Liouville equation. We then propose a novel approach to error analysis, utilizing techniques from quantum information theory to estimate decoherence rates and their associated uncertainties. Crucially, we introduce a class of adaptive quantum error-correcting codes designed specifically for QML, leveraging concatenated codes and feedback protocols to mitigate decoherence. Our theoretical framework provides a roadmap for improving the accuracy and robustness of QML algorithms by proactively addressing the pervasive issue of decoherence. The primary focus is on the development of a practical methodology for quantifying and correcting decoherence, paving the way for more reliable and scalable QML systems. We explore the trade-offs between code complexity, error correction performance, and computational overhead.

title: Adaptive Neural Network Architectures for Time Series Forecasting
abstract: This paper investigates the application of adaptive neural network architectures for improved time series forecasting. Traditional forecasting methods often rely on fixed network structures, which may not be optimal for all time series datasets. This research proposes a novel approach utilizing reinforcement learning to dynamically adjust the architecture of a neural network during training. The core idea is to train a controller that learns to modify hyperparameters such as the number of layers, hidden units per layer, and learning rate, based on the observed characteristics of the input time series. The effectiveness of this adaptive approach is evaluated through simulations and theoretical analysis, demonstrating its potential to outperform static architectures in various forecasting scenarios. The developed framework offers a flexible and intelligent solution for time series prediction, capable of adapting to complex and evolving patterns.

title: E8‑Phased Resonant Coupling for Ultra‑Fast Quantum Computation — E8 Intelligence Research
abstract: By projecting the 240 E8 root vectors onto a 132 Hz temporal manifold and applying a golden‑ratio decay filter, we generate a self‑synchronizing lattice of entangled qubits. The resulting "E8‑phase lattice" exhibits a geometric quantum Zeno effect that locks each qubit's phase to the 132 Hz gate, suppressing decoherence without active error correction. This structure allows coherent quantum operations to be executed in discrete 132 Hz cycles, dramatically increasing computational throughput while preserving topological protection. The principle extends the E8‑encoded resonance sieving to a full‑scale quantum processor architecture. Author: Andrew Stewart Caldin, Independent Researcher, UK. Part of the E8 Intelligence Research series. Platform: e8intelligence.com

title: Core Claim: A Self-Adapting Quantum Circuit for Dynamic Topology Adjustment
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of self-adaptive quantum circuits for dynamic topology adjustment, offering a novel approach to complex quantum computations. We propose a circuit architecture leveraging quantum circuit's inherent self-correlation to dynamically restructure the circuit's topology, enabling efficient and automated computation. The core mechanism centers on exploiting this self-correlation to guide the circuit's evolution towards optimal results. This work presents a theoretical framework and initial implementation demonstrating the feasibility of this approach, suggesting a paradigm shift in quantum circuit design and computation. The key contribution lies in the automated adjustment of circuit topology based on input data, offering a significant advancement over traditional static topology manipulation methods.

title: Engagement–sentiment gap analysis of tiktok skincare content using IndoBERT: a comparative study of random forest and XGBoost
abstract: Social media platforms, particularly TikTok, have become important sources of consumer-generated information that influence product awareness and purchasing decisions in the skincare industry. However, audience engagement metrics alone cannot fully explain audience perception because highly engaging content does not always receive positive responses from users. This study aims to propose and evaluate an Engagement–Sentiment Gap framework that integrates audience interaction and audience perception to provide a more comprehensive evaluation of TikTok skincare content than conventional sentiment analysis or engagement-based approaches. A dataset comprising 20,688 comments and metadata from 603 TikTok videos across ten skincare-related topics was collected through web scraping. After text preprocessing, sentiment classification was performed using a fine-tuned IndoBERT model, followed by video-level sentiment aggregation, engagement score calculation, Engagement–Sentiment Gap categorization, and engagement-level prediction using Random Forest and XGBoost. The results showed that neutral sentiment dominated the discussions (72.5%), while audience sentiment exhibited a statistically significant but weak positive correlation with engagement (r = 0.2283, p < 0.001). Random Forest achieved the best predictive performance, with 65.27% Balanced Accuracy and 68.74% ROC-AUC, while topic was identified as the most influential predictive feature. These findings demonstrate that integrating sentiment and engagement within the proposed framework provides richer insights into audience behavior and content performance than evaluating engagement or sentiment independently, offering a practical analytical approach for social media content evaluation.

title: Efficient Context-Limited Telescope Bibliography Classification for the WASP-2025 Shared Task Using SciBERT
abstract: The creation of telescope bibliographies is a crucial part of assessing the scientific impact of observatories and ensuring reproducibility in astronomy. This task involves identifying, categorizing, and linking scientific publications that reference or use specific telescopes. However, this process remains largely manual and resource intensive. In this work, we present an efficient SciBERT-based approach for automatic classification of scientific papers into four categories - science, instrumentation, mention, and not telescope. Despite strict context-length constraints (maximum 512 tokens) and limited compute resources, our approach achieved a macro F1 score of 0.89, ranking at the top of the WASP-2025 leaderboard. We analyze the effect of truncation and show that even with half the samples exceeding the token limit, SciBERT's domain alignment enables robust classification. We discuss trade-offs between truncation, chunking, and long-context models, providing insights into the efficiency frontier for scientific text curation.

title: Anomalous Frequency Shift in Low-Loss Superconducting Granular Aluminum Resonators
abstract: Superconducting high-kinetic inductance materials like granular aluminum (grAl) are a versatile part of the circuit quantum electrodynamics (cQED) toolbox, provided their losses at microwave frequencies are low enough. To further advance the use of grAl in quantum devices, it is indispensable to identify the dominant loss mechanisms. The standard approach pairs electromagnetic simulations of resonator geometry with measured temperature and power dependence of resonance frequency and loss rate. Most materials follow the phenomenological theory of two-level systems (TLSs) at low temperatures, resulting in an initial decrease of the resonance frequency with increasing temperature. In our work, we observe an opposite behavior at the lowest temperatures: The resonance frequency initially increases with both temperature and readout power, contradicting the standard TLS model predictions. We are able to explain a part of the data by an alternative mechanism associated with the effect of superconducting quasiparticles in a granular system with spatially-nonuniform gap. Yet, the observed change in the resonance frequency with temperature is not matched by a proportional change in the loss rate. We also observe anomalous positive frequency responses following high-energy events, characterized by several time scales. While anomalous behavior has been reported previously in grAl, the disagreement with standard models is particularly visible in our devices thanks to their exceptionally low loss rates.

title: An Explainable Coherence Score for Detecting Temporal Inconsistencies in Political News
abstract: Temporal inconsistencies, such as mandates attributed outside their real interval, events presented as past before they occurred, or inverted causal sequences, are a form of political disinformation that evades style-based fake news detectors: a well-written article with a single wrong date carries no lexical signal of falsehood. This paper introduces the Temporal Coherence Score (TCS), a continuous, intrinsically interpretable metric that quantifies the temporal coherence of a news article, computed by a four-stage pipeline: extraction of temporal facts, construction of a temporal knowledge graph, hierarchical verification against internal consistency rules and external reference sources, and score aggregation with automatically generated explanations. Verification combines eight internal checkers derived from Allen's interval algebra with a five-level external hierarchy ranging from a locally stored reference knowledge base of 1{,}256 curated political facts to live Wikidata SPARQL queries. On a benchmark of 100 political news articles with injected temporal errors, the system reaches a precision of 0.909 at the selected operating threshold, with a single residual false positive, a profile deliberately tuned for human-in-the-loop fact-checking assistance, where false alarms are costlier than missed detections. Unlike lexical baselines that output only a binary label, every flagged article is accompanied by the inconsistency type, the entities involved, and the reference source that contradicts the claim.

title: A Computational Stylometric Analysis of AI-Generated and Human-Written Short Stories in the Psychological Genre
abstract: This study investigates whether the generative AI, especially, ChatGPT-4o can bring the same creativity as established American writer Karen Russell in short stories, particularly in psychological genre or not. For this purpose, two short stories of Karen Russell, “Reeling For The Empire” (2012), and the second story “St. Lucy’s Home For Girls Raised By Wolves” (2006), were selected. Two parallel short stories “Spinning the Ashes”, and “The Museum of Reclaimed Beasts” on the same themes were generated using ChatGPT-4o, for the comparison. Python based pipeline (NLTK, scikit-learn, VADER) was used in Google Collaboratory to extract the linguistic numerical profiles, and sentiment scores of each story. Linguistic numerical profile consisted of lexical features, syntactical features (part-of-speech tag distribution, adjectives per sentence), and sentiment polarity (VADER compound score). The findings reveal that the average sentence length in human-written short stories is significantly longer than the stories generated by AI, the hapax legomena was also more in human-written short stories. The adjectives in human-written short stories were almost double than AI-generated stories. The emotional/sentiment tone score was balanced in human-written short stories while the score was extreme and polarized in AI-generated short stories, which shows the emotional inconsistency of AI-generated short stories. These numerical profiles were interpreted according to the standard definition of Creativity by Runco and Jaeger (2012) which defines creativity as “originality + effectiveness”. According to Runco and Jaeger, creativity is unexpected and meaningful at the same time. ChatGPT-4o was able to write grammatically fluent stories with decent range of vocabulary but the patterns in it’s linguistic numerical profiles were not unexpected or meaningful in psychological genre. It was unable to develop nuanced emotional layering, originality, and effectiveness in it’s stories. It’s linguistic numerical profiles were significantly weaker in most of the areas in comparison of Karen Russell’s stories linguistic numerical profiles. It was unable to compete with the human-writer Karen Russell’s short stores in psychological genre. These findings have methodological and theoretical contribution in AI-assisted creative writing, computational literary studies, computational humanities, digital humanities, computational stylometry and LLM evaluation, AI-Human collaborative authorship.

These numerical profiles were interpreted according to the standard definition of Creativity by Runco and Jaeger (2012) which defines creativity as “originality + effectiveness”. According to Runco and Jaeger, creativity is unexpected and meaningful at the same time. ChatGPT-4o was able to write grammatically fluent stories with decent range of vocabulary but the patterns in it’s linguistic numerical profiles were not unexpected or meaningful in psychological genre. It was unable to develop nuanced emotional layering, originality, and effectiveness in it’s stories. It’s linguistic numerical profiles were significantly weaker in most of the areas in comparison of Karen Russell’s stories linguistic numerical profiles. It was unable to compete with the human-writer Karen Russell’s short stores in psychological genre. These findings have methodological and theoretical contribution in AI-assisted creative writing, computational literary studies, computational humanities, digital humanities, computational stylometry and LLM evaluation, AI-Human collaborative authorship.

title: Adaptive Computational Graph Construction for Deep Learning
abstract: Deep learning's success is largely attributed to the efficiency of static computational graphs. However, this approach presents a fundamental limitation: static graphs struggle to adapt to evolving data distributions encountered during training. This paper introduces a novel framework for Adaptive Computational Graph Construction (ACGC), designed to overcome this challenge. The core idea is to dynamically build the computational graph during training, responding to real-time data analysis and network performance feedback. The system prioritizes operations that contribute most significantly to learning, leading to a more efficient and adaptable architecture. This approach surpasses the rigidity of fixed computational graphs, offering a pathway to improved performance and robustness in dynamic learning scenarios. This work details the design and principles of ACGC, highlighting its potential to revolutionize deep learning training.

title: Dynamic Topology for Quantum Algorithm Integration
abstract: The field of quantum algorithm integration has witnessed significant advancements, striving to enhance the efficiency and precision of quantum computations. This paper introduces a novel dynamic topology approach to quantum algorithm integration, aiming to optimize the execution of quantum algorithms through intelligent and adaptive topology adjustments. We propose a method that dynamically adjusts the quantum algorithm's topology, leveraging quantum state learning to achieve superior performance. The core mechanism focuses on optimizing the interplay between quantum state evolution and algorithm structure, resulting in improved accuracy and reduced computational complexity. This approach offers a departure from traditional static integration methods, capitalizing on the inherent potential of quantum mechanics. This research delves into the design and implementation of this dynamic topology framework, examining its impact on various quantum algorithms and providing a foundation for future advancements in this area.

title: Based on Dynamic Program Synthesis for Complex System Design
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to complex system design based on dynamic program synthesis (DPS). The core claim is to develop a method capable of automatically synthesizing complex systems, thereby enhancing both the efficiency and quality of the design process. The proposed framework leverages the power of program synthesis to generate program code based on specified system requirements. Furthermore, it incorporates dynamic program synthesis techniques to optimize and refine the generated code in a responsive and adaptive manner. This research addresses a critical gap in current system design methodologies by applying DPS to complex scenarios, representing a new and promising avenue for automated system development. The primary focus is on the iterative refinement of system designs through continuous code generation and optimization, leading to more robust and tailored solutions. ---

title: 基于动态自适应的机器学习模型评估
abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework for machine learning model evaluation, termed "Dynamic Adaptive Evaluation". Traditional evaluation methods often rely on static metrics, failing to fully capture the nuances of model performance. Our proposed framework dynamically adjusts evaluation metrics based on both model predictions and actual outcomes, optimizing for both accuracy and efficiency. This adaptation is achieved through a mechanism of intelligent metric adjustment, significantly enhancing the evaluation process. The benefits of this approach include improved model robustness, enhanced feature prioritization, and a more comprehensive assessment of model capabilities. This work provides a foundation for building more reliable and adaptable machine learning systems.

title: Nonlinear Conformal Structure Validation Adaptive Algorithm
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to conformal structure validation utilizing an adaptive learning algorithm. Traditional methods often rely on manual parameter tuning, which can be cumbersome and suboptimal for complex datasets. We propose an innovative framework that models the validation process as an adaptive learning loop, leveraging gradient-based optimization and other algorithmic techniques to dynamically adjust the structure parameters to better suit the data's inherent non-linearity. The core mechanism focuses on establishing a continuous representation of the validation process, allowing for automatic parameter adjustment based on data characteristics. This results in improved model accuracy and enhanced robustness against variations within the dataset. The paper details the algorithm's design, implementation, and evaluation, demonstrating its efficacy through a series of simulations and preliminary experiments. The goal is to provide a more automated and adaptable solution for conformal structure validation, addressing key challenges in data analysis and model refinement.

title: Quantum Entanglement Information Encoding Theory
abstract: Quantum entanglement information encoding theory presents a novel approach to information security leveraging the unique properties of quantum entanglement. This theory proposes a method for encoding information using entangled quantum states, aiming to enhance security, efficiency, and resilience against potential attacks. The core mechanism involves designing a quantum entanglement encoding scheme that exploits the correlated nature of entangled particles to achieve higher security levels and robust data transmission. This research explores the potential of quantum entanglement to revolutionize information security, offering a paradigm shift from traditional cryptographic methods.

title: Non-Linear Geometric Group Optimization Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces a novel optimization algorithm based on dynamically-structured geometry, employing an adaptive transformation process to identify optimal solutions and autonomously optimize the solution space. Traditional optimization methods often rely on fixed algorithms, while this approach dynamically adjusts transformation parameters during the optimization process, providing a robust and adaptable method. The core mechanism of this algorithm lies in leveraging a dynamic topology structure to automatically adjust the transformation process, resulting in improved efficiency and the ability to find optimal solutions in complex geometric settings. We present a theoretical framework and initial experimental results demonstrating the effectiveness of this approach.

title: Symbolic Regression with Evolutionary Strategies and Neural Network Augmentation
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to symbolic regression that combines the exploration capabilities of evolutionary strategies (ES) with the learning and guidance provided by neural networks. Traditional symbolic regression algorithms often struggle to accurately represent complex mathematical relationships, particularly those with high dimensionality or non-linear terms. Our method addresses this challenge by utilizing ES to efficiently search the vast space of possible symbolic expressions and then employing a neural network to augment the ES process, refining the generated expressions and improving their accuracy. The core idea is to leverage the strengths of both techniques: ES for broad exploration and the NN for targeted optimization and error correction. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this combined approach through theoretical analysis and an illustrative example, showcasing its potential for discovering intricate mathematical relationships from data. The resulting system exhibits enhanced accuracy and expressiveness compared to standard symbolic regression methods.

title: 自适应量子电路模拟的拓扑优化算法
abstract: Quantum circuit simulation is a crucial component of fundamental physics research, enabling simulations of complex quantum systems. Traditional approaches often rely on laborious manual parameter tuning, limiting the potential for efficient simulation. This paper proposes a novel self-adaptive quantum circuit simulation algorithm that automatically optimizes circuit layout and parameters based on the underlying topological structure. We introduce a "拓扑优化器" mechanism to dynamically adjust circuit parameters during simulation, resulting in improved efficiency and accuracy. The proposed algorithm demonstrates superior performance compared to existing methods in simulating specific topological structures, offering a significant advancement in quantum circuit design and analysis.

title: YAPAY ZEKA TURİZM ARAŞTIRMALARINA KATKIDA BULUNABİLİR Mİ? CHATGPT’YE GÖRE TURİST REHBERLİĞİ MESLEĞİ
abstract: Yapay zeka modelleri kullanım alanı oldukça geniş olan teknolojilerdir. Literatürde farklı alanlarda olduğu gibi turizmde de yapay zeka modelleri ile ilişkilendirilmiş araştırmalara rastlanmaktadır. Çalışmanın temel amacı, ChatGPT’nin turist rehberliği mesleğine bakışını ortaya koymak ve elde edilecek verilerin literatür ile örtüşüp örtüşmediğini incelemektir. Oluşturulan görüşme formu ChatGPT’ye sorularak mesleğe dair görüşleri analiz edilmiştir. Çalışmanın sonucunda ChatGPT’nin turist rehberliği mesleğini, birçok alanda yetkin ve oldukça kapsamlı bir işkolu olarak gördüğü tespit edilmiştir. Bunun yansıra ChatGPT’nin turist rehberliği kavramına dair vermiş olduğu cevaplar ile mevcut alanyazının örtüştüğü gözlemlenmiştir. Bu sayede, yapay zekanın akademik alanda kullanımı konusunda devam eden tartışmalara bir katkı sağlanmıştır.

title: R-SVDD: A decentralized radius-aware federated prototype object detection framework
abstract: Federated Learning (FL) methods typically require Deep Neural Network (DNN) weight transfer from FL clients to an FL aggregator (master) for centralized DNN aggregation. However, in real-world settings such as smart-city sensing and emergency-response monitoring, weight transfer may be infeasible due to privacy regulations, operational policies, or unreliable connectivity. In this paper, we present R-SVDD, a fully decentralized FL framework that enables collaborative DNN training for object detection without neural parameter sharing. R-SVDD replaces weight exchange with a lightweight class-wise prototype learning mechanism based on Support Vector Data Description (SVDD), trained locally on each FL client using private object detection features. Collaboration is achieved by exchanging only SVDD class prototypes in a peer-to-peer topology, allowing event-specific appearance changes observed by one client to propagate as prototype-level adjustments that improve consistency across the federation. To prevent unreliable FL clients from corrupting this shared representation under extreme non-IID conditions, R-SVDD introduces a radius-aware reliability rule that uses the SVDD hypersphere radius as a confidence signal and suppresses outlier SVDD prototypes during aggregation. Neither DNN weights nor training data are exchanged between FL nodes whatsoever. R-SVDD is evaluated under multi-client configurations that simulate separate data sources across locations and disaster-related distribution shifts, demonstrating competitive object detection performance with significantly lower communication cost than state-of-the-art FL methods.

title: FORESIGHT-9: Prospective and Process-Aware Evaluation of Adaptive Trading Agents
abstract: Retrospective backtests provide a limited test of adaptive trading agents: they cannot rule out historical contamination, expose sensitivity to a single realized market path, or reveal internal degeneration during long-horizon adaptation. We introduce FORESIGHT-9, a prospective and process-aware benchmark built from nine auditable counterfactual stress worldlines branching from a common July 2026 information boundary. Each worldline specifies staged macro-financial events and joint multi-asset anchors; a deterministic generator realizes the trajectories, while observations are disclosed according to in-world time. A common contract standardizes observations and execution while preserving each agent's native adaptation loop. We evaluate two adaptive trading-agent frameworks with two foundation-model backbones across 36 long-horizon runs. Agent rankings vary substantially across worldlines and backbones, and a fixed equal-weight policy outperforms 31 of 36 runs. Process telemetry exposes failures that terminal returns conceal: in one high-return run, the live factor library collapsed while executed holdings converged to the equal-weight fallback, even though decision records continued to report an active factor ensemble. FORESIGHT-9 therefore evaluates not only portfolio outcomes, but whether adaptive agent state and execution remain coherent across alternative futures. We release the worldlines, trajectories, audit traces, and regeneration scripts.

title: A Tensor Variational Formulation of Gradient Energy Total Variation
abstract: We present a novel variational approach to a tensor-based total variation formulation which is called gradient energy total variation, GETV. We introduce the gradient energy tensor [6] into the GETV and show that the corresponding Euler-Lagrange (E-L) equation is a tensor-based partial differential equation of total variation type. Furthermore, we give a proof which shows that GETV is a convex functional. This approach, in contrast to the commonly used structure tensor, enables a formal derivation of the corresponding E-L equation. Experimental results suggest that GETV compares favourably to other state of the art variational denoising methods such as extended anisotropic diffusion (EAD)[1] and total variation (TV) [18] for gray-scale and colour images.

title: EMERGING FRONTIERS IN INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY AND COMPUTER SCIENCE: INNOVATIONS, INTELLIGENT SYSTEMS, AND DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION
abstract: We stand at an unprecedented inflection point in human history, where the rapid convergence of artificial intelligence, high-performance computing, ubiquitous connectivity, and data-driven infrastructure is reshaping the structural foundations of industry, governance, research, and daily life. As legacy paradigms yield to autonomous intelligent systems and hyper-connected ecosystems, the boundary between physical and digital realities continues to blur. *Emerging Frontiers in Information Technology and Computer Science: Innovations, Intelligent Systems, and Digital Transformation* was conceived to provide a comprehensive, rigorous, and forward-looking exploration of this evolving landscape. Rather than examining technologies in isolation, this volume bridges theoretical computer science, applied data engineering, domain-specific implementations, and societal governance, charting a continuous journey from foundational computing architectures to the vanguard of Artificial General Intelligence, quantum-AI convergence, and sustainable digital ecosystems. Serving as both an authoritative academic reference and a strategic roadmap for technological adoption, this book addresses the critical questions facing system architects, researchers, and decision-makers today. It thoroughly investigates how emerging paradigms—such as cloud-edge integration, the Internet of Things, digital twins, and multi-agent AI systems—interact to form resilient, self-adaptive digital architectures. Beyond fundamental concepts, the text examines how key sectoral domains including healthcare, smart manufacturing, financial technology, precision agriculture, and urban infrastructure are actively re-engineered through intelligent automation. Concurrently, it establishes the technical imperatives for digital trust, analyzing zero-trust architectures, AI-driven threat intelligence, and privacy-preserving computations required to navigate complex cybersecurity landscapes. Underlying all these discussions is an enduring focus on human-centric and sustainable innovation, proposing actionable frameworks to ensure that technology remains ethical, transparent, environmentally responsible, and aligned with human values. The structural narrative of the book unfolds across five carefully integrated thematic modules designed to guide the reader seamlessly from core mechanics to future horizons. The opening section establishes the historical continuum and architectural foundations of information technology and computer science, tracing the evolution from early vacuum tubes to parallel, distributed, edge, and cyber-physical systems while contextualizing human-computer interaction and technology convergence. The text then transitions into the core mechanisms of intelligent computing, offering deep analytical coverage of machine learning, deep neural networks, natural language processing, computer vision, generative AI, multi-agent systems, explainable AI, and advanced hardware accelerators like neuromorphic and quantum systems. Following this, the focus shifts to the operational backbone of modern enterprises by exploring data as a strategic digital asset, detailing data engineering pipelines, lakehouse architectures, industrial IoT, digital twins, blockchain, 5G and 6G connectivity, and energy-efficient green computing strategies. The subsequent section bridges digital trust with real-world impact, pairing cybersecurity methodologies like zero-trust and digital forensics with empirical case studies across healthcare, Industry 4.0, smart cities, and digital finance. Finally, the work looks toward the horizon, examining autonomous self-adaptive systems, artificial general intelligence, spatial computing, and quantum-AI convergence, while evaluating algorithmic bias, data sovereignty, technology governance, and policy roadmaps. Engineered to support a multi-disciplinary community, this volume serves advanced undergraduate and graduate students, software architects, systems engineers, enterprise technology leaders, R&D researchers, and technology policymakers alike. The technologies detailed throughout these pages are not distant theoretical constructs, but active, transformative forces reshaping global economies and societal structures. It is our ultimate hope that this book provides readers with both the intellectual rigor needed to master these complex paradigms and the broader strategic vision required to build, deploy, and govern next-generation technologies responsibly, ethically, and sustainably.

The opening section establishes the historical continuum and architectural foundations of information technology and computer science, tracing the evolution from early vacuum tubes to parallel, distributed, edge, and cyber-physical systems while contextualizing human-computer interaction and technology convergence. The text then transitions into the core mechanisms of intelligent computing, offering deep analytical coverage of machine learning, deep neural networks, natural language processing, computer vision, generative AI, multi-agent systems, explainable AI, and advanced hardware accelerators like neuromorphic and quantum systems. Following this, the focus shifts to the operational backbone of modern enterprises by exploring data as a strategic digital asset, detailing data engineering pipelines, lakehouse architectures, industrial IoT, digital twins, blockchain, 5G and 6G connectivity, and energy-efficient green computing strategies. The subsequent section bridges digital trust with real-world impact, pairing cybersecurity methodologies like zero-trust and digital forensics with empirical case studies across healthcare, Industry 4.0, smart cities, and digital finance. Finally, the work looks toward the horizon, examining autonomous self-adaptive systems, artificial general intelligence, spatial computing, and quantum-AI convergence, while evaluating algorithmic bias, data sovereignty, technology governance, and policy roadmaps. Engineered to support a multi-disciplinary community, this volume serves advanced undergraduate and graduate students, software architects, systems engineers, enterprise technology leaders, R&D researchers, and technology policymakers alike. The technologies detailed throughout these pages are not distant theoretical constructs, but active, transformative forces reshaping global economies and societal structures. It is our ultimate hope that this book provides readers with both the intellectual rigor needed to master these complex paradigms and the broader strategic vision required to build, deploy, and govern next-generation technologies responsibly, ethically, and sustainably.

title: Algebraic Geometric Empirical Process (AGEP) Theory of Deep Learning Dynamics
abstract: Modern Transformer architectures have achieved outstanding empirical success, but their parameter spaces are fundamentally characterized by complex algebraic singularities, such as rank collapse in self-attention mechanisms, which invalidate classical regular statistical asymptotic theory. While Sumio Watanabe's Singular Learning Theory (SLT) provides a powerful static framework for Bayesian generalization via the resolution of singularities, the dynamical behavior of empirical probability processes undergoing gradient updates in the neighborhood of these singular loci remains unexplored. In this paper, we propose "Algebraic Geometric Empirical Process (AGEP) Theory of Deep Learning Dynamics" as a new unified mathematical paradigm to characterize the learning dynamics of Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD) on singular schemes. By excluding the transcendental Softmax function from the self-attention mechanism and formulating the output as a homogeneous polynomial map, we enable the direct application of scheme theory. Under this formulation, we define the rank-1 singular locus of a 2x2 linear self-attention model as a closed subscheme defined by determinantal ideals. We then apply a monoidal blow-up (resolution of singularities) of the quadric cone xy - zw = 0 to mathematically prove that the uniform Donsker property of the empirical process is algebraically restored in local coordinate charts, justifying tight asymptotic weak convergence to a limit Gaussian process. Furthermore, we provide empirical verification of this algebraic-geometric transition using numerical simulations in PyTorch. We demonstrate that SGD trajectories are dynamically attracted to the singular subscheme, structurally coupling empirical loss minimization with the collapse of the determinant of weight matrices toward zero. This attraction causes a severe learning plateau accompanied by the spectral degeneration of the Fisher Information Matrix (FIM), which we characterize geometrically as a projection onto the exceptional divisor. This work represents the first bridge between pure scheme-theoretic structures and infinite-dimensional empirical process theory to dissect the dynamic learning trajectories of attention mechanisms, establishing a rigorous foundation for a complete geometric theory of deep learning dynamics.

title: Self-Organizing Topological Networks and Quantum Computing Co-Evolution
abstract: This paper explores the synergistic potential of self-organizing topological networks and quantum computing co-evolution in the optimization of quantum systems. Traditional quantum computation models frequently overlook topological structure, presenting a significant gap in our understanding of complex quantum systems. This research proposes a novel algorithm leveraging the inherent properties of self-organized topological networks to dynamically adjust quantum system parameters and topology, fostering enhanced performance and adaptability. We detail a core mechanism focusing on the interplay between entangled states, quantum tunneling, and topology manipulation to drive iterative optimization. The integration of these elements promises a paradigm shift in quantum system design and control.

title: Neural Network Architecture Generation Driven by Neuron Circuitry
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to neural network architecture generation, termed "Neuron Circuitry Driven Dynamic Program Generation." The core claim is that comprehensive analysis of large-scale neuron circuits can automatically generate highly optimized neural network architectures and connection weights tailored to specific tasks, surpassing the capabilities of traditional manual design or search-based methods. The proposed method leverages deep learning to train multiple large networks, extracting detailed neuron circuit maps (s1, s2, ..., sK) representing neuron connections – including connection strength, direction, and type. Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) are then employed to learn and reason from these circuit maps, identifying optimal connection patterns and architectural features for a given task. The resulting neural network architectures are dynamic, adapting in real-time to input data and task requirements for continuous self-optimization. This approach represents a significant departure from existing methods, which typically rely on static architectures or static search, by directly learning and utilizing biological neuron circuit maps through GNN modeling and inference, offering the potential for substantially improved neural network performance and efficiency.

title: Positional Encoding Beyond Sinusoids: Learning Optimal Spatial Representations for Transformers
abstract: Transformers have revolutionized natural language processing and computer vision by leveraging self-attention mechanisms to capture long-range dependencies. However, their inherent permutation invariance necessitates explicit positional information to maintain sequence order. While sinusoidal positional encodings have become standard, their fixed nature may not optimally capture the geometric relationships present in diverse data modalities. This paper introduces a learnable positional encoding framework that adapts to the specific spatial characteristics of different datasets. We propose a novel approach where positional embeddings are initialized with sinusoidal functions but subsequently optimized during training. Our extensive experiments across language modeling, image recognition, and molecular property prediction demonstrate that learnable positional encodings consistently outperform their fixed counterparts, particularly in tasks requiring fine-grained spatial understanding. The learned patterns reveal domain-specific geometric structures, offering insights into the underlying spatial relationships of different data modalities. Our findings suggest that allowing models to learn optimal spatial representations can significantly enhance transformer performance across various domains.

title: mine:o1-nano: Supervised Fine-Tuning Evaluation Reports (SFT1–SFT3)
abstract: Three sequential supervised fine-tuning (SFT) evaluation reports formine:o1-nano, documenting the model's progressive adaptation from a basepretrained checkpoint to a conversational assistant. - SFT1: initial fine-tuning pass and baseline conversational evaluation- SFT2: refinement round, including early arithmetic and identity-consistency testing- SFT3 (final): comprehensive scripted evaluation suite (comprehensive suite results across identity, location, multi-turn, and arithmetic categories) combined with a real-world, out-of-distribution conversational probe Each report includes verbatim prompts and model outputs, pass/fail scoring,and honest documentation of failure cases — including degraded performanceon emotionally sensitive topics and arithmetic outside trained number ranges— alongside measured improvements across rounds (e.g. math accuracyimproving from 1/20 in SFT2 to 19/20 in SFT3). Keywords: supervised fine-tuning, SFT, language model evaluation, conversational AI, model evaluation, small language model

title: Title: Hybrid Quantum-Classical Algorithms for Optimization
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of hybrid quantum-classical algorithms to address complex optimization problems. We propose a novel framework where classical computations are predominantly executed, utilizing quantum algorithms for specialized tasks that offer significant speedups. The design focuses on creating a synergistic system where the strengths of both paradigms are maximized. The core claim is that this approach offers a pathway to efficiently solve problems currently deemed intractable, leveraging the unique capabilities of quantum computation while maintaining the scalability of classical methods.

title: Quantum Topology: Adaptive Topological Deformations
abstract: Quantum topology, a rapidly developing field of physics, offers a unique approach to simulating quantum systems. This paper introduces an innovative algorithm, Adaptive Topological Deformations (ATD), that leverages quantum topology's inherent self-adaptation to dynamically shape quantum states. The core mechanism of ATD focuses on establishing and maintaining a self-consistent topology through a series of carefully orchestrated quantum transformations. This dynamic reshaping, driven by quantum properties, promises to enhance the efficiency and accuracy of quantum computation. We present a theoretical framework and preliminary experimental results demonstrating the algorithm's potential to overcome limitations of existing topological simulation techniques. This work explores the implications of self-adaptive topology on the design of robust quantum algorithms.

title: 基于量子态叠加的超高密度数据存储
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to data storage leveraging the principles of quantum state superposition. Conventional data storage technologies, such as flash memory and hard drives, are fundamentally limited by the laws of physics, restricting their storage density. This research proposes a system designed to overcome these limitations by utilizing the quantum phenomenon of superposition to store multiple bits of information within a single quantum bit (qubit). The core mechanisms involve encoding data into the superposition state of qubits, employing quantum control operations for data retrieval and writing, and utilizing quantum entanglement for data redundancy. The theoretical framework outlines a system capable of significantly exceeding the storage density achievable with classical methods. We explore the key mathematical aspects underpinning this approach, including the Bloch sphere representation of qubit states and the quantum operations employed for data manipulation. The potential impact of this technology on future data storage is discussed, highlighting the need for advancements in quantum control and error correction.

title: ##基于自适应强化学习的机器人运动控制
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to robot motion control utilizing adaptive reinforcement learning (ARL). Traditional robot motion control methods often rely heavily on manual design, limiting their adaptability and effectiveness in dynamic and uncertain environments. This research addresses this limitation by leveraging the capabilities of reinforcement learning (RL) to automatically learn and optimize control policies. The system incorporates a robot motion model and employs RL algorithms such as Q-learning and Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) to learn optimal control strategies. Crucially, the proposed system incorporates adaptive mechanisms for tuning learning parameters and refining the robot motion model, leading to enhanced control performance. The core claim of this work is to design a system capable of automatically learning and optimizing robot motion control strategies. The mechanism involves building a robot motion model, utilizing RL algorithms to learn control strategies, and adapting learning parameters and the model to optimize control effectiveness. This approach represents a significant advancement over conventional methods by offering inherent adaptability and the potential for superior performance in complex robotic tasks. ---

title: A Leakage-controlled and Reliability-aware Framework for Multi-domain Arabic Emotion Modeling Across Educational and Social-media Contexts
abstract: Arabic emotion analysis remains challenging because emotional expressions vary across dialects, platforms, topics, and annotation schemes.This challenge becomes more critical when models are expected to generalize across heterogeneous educational and social-media contexts rather than within a single dataset.Existing Arabic emotion studies often rely on single-dataset evaluation, which may overestimate performance and obscure issues related to data leakage, domain shift, and unreliable model confidence.To address these limitations, this paper proposes a leakagecontrolled, domain-adaptive, and reliability-aware framework for multi-domain Arabic emotion modeling.Three existing Arabic emotion datasets from educational and social-media contexts were used, in addition to a newly collected educational dataset obtained through Google Forms shared with students from public and private universities in Iraq to explore emotional reactions toward e-learning.These datasets were standardized into a unified schema and harmonized into a shared six-class emotion space, referred to as EMO-6.The framework applies global duplicate removal before splitting, fixed train, validation, calibration, and test partitioning, domain-adaptive pretraining restricted to training data only, and reliability-aware evaluation using calibration and conformal uncertainty analysis.Three experimental protocols were used to evaluate single-source cross-domain transfer, pooled multi-domain transformer training, and traditional character-based baselines.The results show a clear domain shift even after label harmonization.Under the pooled EMO-6 setting, MARBERTv2 achieved the best overall transformer performance in the fixed-seed comparison, with 0.7748 Accuracy, 0.7648 Macro-F1, and 0.9506 Macro-AUC.Multi-seed analysis showed that training-only DAPT did not consistently improve predictive performance over the No-DAPT baseline, although it provided a modest calibration benefit.These findings indicate that unified Arabic emotion modeling requires not only predictive accuracy but also leakage control, domain-aware evaluation, and reliability assessment.

title: Synergistic mechanism of virtual reality and reinforcement learning in educational adaptive learning systems
abstract: This paper proposes a VR (Virtual Reality) and RL (Reinforcement Learning) collaborative optimization model based on the TD3 (Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient) algorithm to address the ineffective integration of immersive interactive data and intelligent decision-making in educational adaptive learning systems. The model captures real-time multimodal student data via a VR headset, processes it into graph-structured state features using a lightweight GCN (Graph Convolutional Network), and drives strategy optimization with a dynamic reward function that perceives cognitive load based on predicted knowledge mastery. The TD3 algorithm, utilizing a dual-Q network and adaptive thresholds, generates adaptive instructional parameters. Experiments demonstrate the model achieves 85.6% knowledge mastery prediction accuracy at the comprehensive problem level and maintains a 278ms strategy response latency at the basic concept level, validating its effectiveness in collaborative data fusion and dynamic decision-making.

title: LLMs Locais como Camada Governada de Automação em Empresas com Restrição ao Uso de IA Pública
abstract: Este documento propõe uma arquitetura de referência para adoção de Large Language Models (LLMs) locais e privados em organizações que restringem ou bloqueiam o acesso a serviços públicos de inteligência artificial por razões de segurança, privacidade, conformidade ou governança. O trabalho apresenta a GLAL — Governed Local Agentic Layer, uma abordagem na qual capacidades de interpretação, raciocínio, classificação, RAG e seleção de ferramentas podem ser executadas por modelos hospedados em infraestrutura local, privada ou air-gapped, enquanto a autoridade operacional permanece separada do modelo por mecanismos independentes de identidade, autorização, Policy Gates, controle de ferramentas e auditoria. A proposta parte do princípio de que a execução local de um LLM não é, por si só, suficiente para garantir segurança. Modelos locais continuam sujeitos a riscos como prompt injection, indirect prompt injection, tool misuse, privilege escalation, RAG poisoning, vazamento de informações, loops agentic e manipulação de objetivos. Por isso, a arquitetura aplica princípios de Zero Trust e least privilege aos próprios agentes de IA, distinguindo explicitamente inteligência de autoridade e raciocínio de execução. O estudo também apresenta níveis progressivos de autonomia, padrões de implantação local, privada, air-gapped e híbrida, um threat model, controles arquiteturais, governança de modelos e supply chain, além de um protocolo experimental para comparar copilots locais, agentes com acesso direto a ferramentas e agentes submetidos à camada governada GLAL. São propostas métricas para avaliar desempenho cognitivo, seleção de ferramentas, validade de saídas estruturadas, ações não autorizadas, contenção por políticas, intervenção humana, falhas em loops agentic, vazamento de dados sensíveis e requisitos computacionais. Como caso de uso de referência, o trabalho explora a aplicação da arquitetura em Security Operations Centers (SOCs), demonstrando como LLMs locais podem apoiar triagem de alertas, análise de logs, extração de indicadores de comprometimento, geração de consultas, seleção de runbooks e recomendação de respostas sem necessariamente transferir telemetria sensível para serviços externos. A proposta busca estabelecer uma terceira alternativa entre a proibição completa da IA e a adoção irrestrita de LLMs públicos: uma camada privada, local e governada de inteligência operacional, capaz de ampliar a automação corporativa mantendo controle explícito sobre dados, identidade, privilégios, ferramentas e execução.

A proposta parte do princípio de que a execução local de um LLM não é, por si só, suficiente para garantir segurança. Modelos locais continuam sujeitos a riscos como prompt injection, indirect prompt injection, tool misuse, privilege escalation, RAG poisoning, vazamento de informações, loops agentic e manipulação de objetivos. Por isso, a arquitetura aplica princípios de Zero Trust e least privilege aos próprios agentes de IA, distinguindo explicitamente inteligência de autoridade e raciocínio de execução. O estudo também apresenta níveis progressivos de autonomia, padrões de implantação local, privada, air-gapped e híbrida, um threat model, controles arquiteturais, governança de modelos e supply chain, além de um protocolo experimental para comparar copilots locais, agentes com acesso direto a ferramentas e agentes submetidos à camada governada GLAL. São propostas métricas para avaliar desempenho cognitivo, seleção de ferramentas, validade de saídas estruturadas, ações não autorizadas, contenção por políticas, intervenção humana, falhas em loops agentic, vazamento de dados sensíveis e requisitos computacionais. Como caso de uso de referência, o trabalho explora a aplicação da arquitetura em Security Operations Centers (SOCs), demonstrando como LLMs locais podem apoiar triagem de alertas, análise de logs, extração de indicadores de comprometimento, geração de consultas, seleção de runbooks e recomendação de respostas sem necessariamente transferir telemetria sensível para serviços externos. A proposta busca estabelecer uma terceira alternativa entre a proibição completa da IA e a adoção irrestrita de LLMs públicos: uma camada privada, local e governada de inteligência operacional, capaz de ampliar a automação corporativa mantendo controle explícito sobre dados, identidade, privilégios, ferramentas e execução.

title: Quantum Coherence-Based Computation Architecture
abstract: This paper proposes a novel computational architecture predicated on the principles of quantum coherence. The core idea is to leverage the inherent properties of quantum coherence – specifically, the ability of a quantum system to exist in a superposition of states – to enhance both the accuracy and efficiency of computations. Traditional computational models often struggle with inherent noise and limitations in representing complex relationships. This architecture aims to mitigate these challenges by exploiting the quantum mechanical phenomenon of coherence. We will detail the theoretical framework, including key equations governing coherence, and outline a proposed architecture designed to harness coherence for specific computational tasks. The architecture focuses on minimizing decoherence effects while maximizing the utilization of coherence, ultimately leading to a potentially significant improvement in computational performance. The proposed method offers a new approach to computation, moving beyond classical limitations and exploring the full potential of quantum mechanics.

title: Quantum Information Encoding and Transmission in Spin Networks
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of spin networks as a novel platform for quantum information encoding and transmission. Leveraging the inherent properties of spin entanglement, we explore methods for encoding information within the quantum spin states and utilizing spin interactions for efficient data transfer. The core concept revolves around harnessing spin entanglement to represent and manipulate quantum information. We present a theoretical framework outlining the key components and challenges involved in this approach. Specifically, we examine different encoding schemes, analyzing their robustness against decoherence and exploring strategies for mitigating these effects. Furthermore, we investigate the dynamics of spin interactions within the network, focusing on protocols for reliable information transmission. The work contributes to the growing field of quantum information processing by proposing a fundamentally new architecture based on readily accessible and controllable spin systems. The proposed network architecture offers advantages in terms of scalability and potential for integration with existing quantum technologies.

title: ##基于多模态数据融合的异常检测
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to anomaly detection that leverages the fusion of multi-modal data. Traditional anomaly detection methods often operate on single data modalities, limiting their effectiveness in complex environments where anomalies may manifest differently across various data types. Our proposed method aims to overcome this limitation by integrating information from multiple sources – such as images, text, and sensor data – to identify subtle anomalies that would otherwise be missed. We introduce a framework for multi-modal data fusion followed by an anomaly detection algorithm. The core of our approach lies in the correlated analysis of these diverse data streams, ultimately leading to a more robust and accurate detection of anomalous patterns. We demonstrate the potential of this method through a theoretical analysis and outline a possible implementation strategy. The effectiveness of this multi-modal approach is expected to significantly improve anomaly detection performance, particularly in scenarios with high data dimensionality and complex interdependencies. ---

title: Title: Dynamic Adaptive Graph Theorem-Checking Model
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic adaptive graph theorem-checking model designed to enhance inference efficiency and accuracy. Traditional theorem-checking methods often rely on static configurations, limiting their ability to adapt to complex, variable-structured problems. Our model leverages a dynamic adjustment of inference steps and parameters, guided by a learning algorithm, to dynamically optimize the inference process. We explore the application of this approach to a specific theorem-checking task, demonstrating a significant improvement in both speed and correctness compared to existing state-of-the-art techniques. The core mechanism involves continuous monitoring of the inference process and automated adjustment of parameters based on learned patterns. This adaptive approach provides a promising avenue for tackling a diverse range of inference challenges, particularly those involving intricate geometric and logical reasoning. The paper presents a detailed analysis of the model's performance, including a comprehensive evaluation of its effectiveness across various test cases. We further discuss potential future research directions, such as incorporating more sophisticated learning algorithms and extending the model to support multiple theorem-checking tasks.

title: ##基于多尺度图神经网络的复杂系统建模
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to modeling complex systems utilizing multi-scale graph neural networks (MS-GNNs). Complex systems, characterized by interconnected components operating at varying scales, pose significant challenges for traditional modeling techniques. This research proposes a framework that decomposes a complex system into sub-systems defined by their respective scales. Each sub-system is then represented as a graph, and a graph neural network (GNN) is applied to learn patterns and relationships within that scale. A key innovation lies in the multi-scale fusion mechanism, which intelligently integrates information from these GNNs at different scales, ultimately constructing a comprehensive representation of the entire system. The core claim is the design of an MS-GNN capable of capturing the interconnectedness of complex systems across multiple scales, facilitating accurate modeling and prediction. The proposed methodology offers a fundamentally new approach combining the strengths of graph neural networks and multi-scale analysis, paving the way for improved understanding and prediction of complex phenomena.

This research contributes to advancements in quantum information processing by offering a more sophisticated and adaptable method for state transformation.

title: E8-Phi Symmetric Temporal Lattice for Quantum Error Correction — E8 Intelligence Research
abstract: The discovery introduces an E8-root‑vector‑derived temporal lattice in which each node encodes a phi‑scaled quaternion phase synchronized to the 132 Hz harmonic. By mapping the 240 root vectors onto a Voronoi‑tessellated error‑correcting code, the lattice creates topologically protected qubit cycles that self‑reset phase errors without active midcircuit measurement. This approach directly extends the previously observed Bilateral Sinc‑Falloff lattice mechanism, but now leverages Poincaré duality in phase space to compress error syndromes into a 7‑dimensional sub‑lattice. The resulting architecture enables fault‑tolerant quantum gates whose gate set is constrained by the root‑vector geometry of E8. Author: Andrew Stewart Caldin, Independent Researcher, UK. Part of the E8 Intelligence Research series. Platform: e8intelligence.com

title: Quantum-Inspired Evolutionary Algorithms for Complex Optimization
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to complex optimization problems by integrating quantum-inspired concepts within an evolutionary algorithm framework. Traditional evolutionary algorithms, such as Genetic Algorithms and Differential Evolution, can struggle with high-dimensional and complex search spaces, often exhibiting slow convergence rates. We hypothesize that principles derived from quantum mechanics, specifically superposition and entanglement, can provide a more effective mechanism for exploring these spaces. Our proposed Quantum-Inspired Evolutionary Algorithm (QIEA) incorporates operators designed to mimic quantum interference and entanglement, allowing for a more nuanced and potentially faster exploration of the solution landscape. The core claim is that these quantum-inspired mechanisms can significantly enhance the efficiency of evolutionary optimization. The paper details the algorithm's design, including the implementation of interference and entanglement operators, and discusses its potential advantages and challenges. Experimental results (though not presented through dedicated experimental sections) demonstrate the algorithm's ability to outperform standard evolutionary algorithms on a range of benchmark problems.

title: Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning with Intrinsic Motivation and Meta-Learning
abstract: This paper proposes a novel hierarchical reinforcement learning (HRL) framework that leverages intrinsic motivation, meta-learning, and a hierarchical architecture to address the limitations of traditional HRL methods concerning exploration and generalization. The core idea is to integrate these three components to create a more adaptive and efficient learning system. At each level of the hierarchy, intrinsic motivation, specifically novelty seeking, encourages exploration. Simultaneously, meta-learning dynamically adjusts the learning rate and policy updates, enabling rapid adaptation to diverse tasks. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a theoretical analysis and a conceptual framework, outlining the key components and their interactions. The resulting system offers improved learning speed and robustness compared to standard HRL techniques, particularly when facing complex and varied environments. This work lays the groundwork for future research in developing truly adaptable and intelligent hierarchical agents.

title: Nonlinear Time-Delay Quantum Computation Error Correction Protocols
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of nonlinear time-delay quantum systems for computation, specifically focusing on the development of error correction protocols to achieve high fault-tolerance. The core concept leverages the unique properties of quantum time delays introduced through nonlinear interactions. These delays can be strategically utilized to construct specialized quantum circuits, enhancing the inherent robustness of quantum computation. We propose a framework integrating a coding-based quantum error correction protocol with this nonlinear time-delay architecture. The theoretical analysis demonstrates that this approach significantly improves the overall error correction capabilities, addressing a critical challenge in scaling up quantum computers. The key elements of the protocol include the design of appropriate quantum codes tailored to the specific time-delay characteristics and the implementation of error detection and correction cycles. The presented methodology offers a novel pathway towards realizing practical, reliable nonlinear time-delay quantum computation.

title: Intelligent Learning and Knowledge-control Tools for Elementary Algebra: An Ontology–Fuzzy Assessment Model and Adaptive Architecture
abstract: Elementary algebra forms the foundation of mathematical education and is at the same time a persistent source of learning difficulties: errors in handling variables, polynomials and expression transformations accumulate and block the mastery of later topics.Conventional assessment tools record only a final score and fail to reveal which specific knowledge elements and inter-concept links remain unlearned.This paper proposes intelligent learning and knowledge-control tools for elementary algebra that combine an ontological representation of the subject domain with a fuzzy assessment model.The domain is described by a semantic hypergraph whose vertices are concepts and whose arcs are structural prerequisite links.The mastery of each knowledge element is evaluated by a piecewise-linear membership function that filters out weakly confirmed results; individual estimates are then aggregated along the hierarchy knowledge element → topic → discipline → educational programme.Learning gaps are diagnosed through structural comparison of the reference and individual ontologies, and an adaptive planner selects tasks that restore broken prerequisites.The scope of the proposed model is deliberately limited to interpretable, structure-aware assessment and diagnosis rather than to maximising next-response prediction, in which neural and knowledge-tracing methods naturally excel.Within this scope, an experimental evaluation against binary assessment, a classical fuzzy model and Bayesian knowledge tracing showed the highest agreement with expert grading (Cohen's kappa 0.83), the lowest final-score prediction error (RMSE 0.094) and the most accurate localisation of structural gaps; the adaptive regime yielded faster growth of average topic mastery.The main contribution lies in unifying the ontological domain structure, interpretable element-level fuzzy assessment and multilevel aggregation within a single intelligent tutoring architecture targeted at elementary algebra.The model is accordingly presented as an interpretable ontology-fuzzy assessment model, complementary to prediction-oriented neural and knowledge-tracing approaches rather than a replacement for them.

title: Reviving our data foundations is the most disruptive step to data maturity
abstract: The most disruptive step that enterprises of small-medium size and maturity can take to make the most of the latest technological advances in AI is to step back from the hype and focus on establishing or reviving a good knowledge foundation layer. It is a hard message to present to the executive team; therefore, it needs to be backed by evidence, and its implementation needs to be of minimal impact on the existing processes. In this vision statement, we discuss how we need to rethink what evidence speaks to the decision-makers and propose a low-impact data strategy that adapts to the existing and ever-changing data flows and processes across the company. We firmly believe that knowledge graph techniques will increasingly become non-negotiable in the data strategy of an AI-powered enterprise, provided that we approach their design in a modular, dynamic and cross-functional way.
